articles.summary: Have Chelsea shown themselves as the biggest threat to Manchester City’s title defence?
articles.body:
Radio 5 Live , · 28 Sep 2026 , · 43 mins

Ben and Ellen are joined by Em Sanders to dissect a fiery London derby at Stamford Bridge, where Chelsea claimed bragging rights over Arsenal. The team examine Arsenal’s early-season stumbling blocks ahead of a huge week featuring away trips to Paris FC and Manchester City. Plus, hear post-match reaction from Sonia Bompastor and Lucy Bronze, who give credit to Katie McCabe and Lexi Potter, who could be England’s next breakthrough star ahead of Sarina Wiegman’s Lionesses squad announcement on Tuesday. Ellen, Ben and Em also assess Tottenham’s unbeaten start to the WSL season and whether they can maintain their form against tougher opposition, before looking ahead to Matchday 2 of the Women’s Champions League. articles.title: Adu sube la apuesta
articles.standfirst: El bilbaíno ha dado un paso al frente en este inicio de curso. Interpreta mejor el juego, su toma de decisiones ha mejorado y está siendo diferencial en el último tercio del campo
articles.summary: El bilbaíno ha dado un paso al frente en este inicio de curso. Interpreta mejor el juego, su toma de decisiones ha mejorado y está siendo diferencial en el último tercio del campo.
articles.body: Malcom Adu Ares (Bilbao, 2001) llegó al Eibar hace un año escaso para vivir tardes como la de ayer ante Las Palmas. El futbolista bilbaíno firmó uno de sus mejores encuentros con la elástica armera para elevar a Jokin Aranbarri a los altares y ser el primer técnico en la historia del club que logra seis victorias consecutivas en el fútbol profesional. Un logro de todo el grupo, pero en el que Adu tiene una cuota importante de responsabilidad. El ex del Athletic ha encontrado en el sector derecho el lugar donde explotar todas sus virtudes. Actuó durante gran parte de la pasada campaña por la izquierda y en la primera jornada también estuvo escorado en ese perfil en un encuentro en el que no tuvo su día y acabó silbado por un sector de Ipurua. Sin embargo, en un mes le ha dado la vuelta a la situación y se ha convertido en una pieza fundamental dentro del engranaje ofensivo de Aranbarri, llenando el vacío que dejó la marcha de Corpas al Albacete. Adu está volando y el Eibar se agarra a sus alas para continuar en lo más alto de la tabla. Encadena cuatro titularidades y en todas ellas ha dado muestras de su repertorio. Con una clara mejoría en la toma de decisiones y sabiendo interpretar el ritmo que requiere cada jugada, el vizcaíno está siendo diferencial en el último tercio del campo y en apenas seis partidos ya ha superado los registros de la pasada temporada, en la que sólo hizo dos goles y dio una asistencia. El plan de Aranbarri ante Las Palmas pasaba por empezar los ataques desde la izquierda para acabar en la derecha. Arbilla dio una exhibición con sus diagonales y las dudas de Iván Jaime y Loiodice permitieron al Eibar acumular muchas llegadas de peligro por el sector derecho, donde Álvaro y Adu se entendieron a la perfección para atacar la profundidad. El defensa volvió a marcar y el 18 dio dos asistencias en apenas cuatro minutos que desnivelaron la balanza a favor de su equipo. La apuesta que hizo el pasado verano César Palacios por Adu era a largo plazo. Y en su segundo año en Ipurua, el canterano del Athletic ha subido claramente sus prestaciones. Como hicieron la pasada temporada Magunagoitia o Guruzeta. Dar continuidad a estas sensaciones es el objetivo para esta temporada de un jugador cuestionado durante algunas fases del pasado curso, pero que reúne un talento descomunal para tener una influencia directa en el juego del Eibar.

articles.title: El Girona tiene una lista de bajas que mete miedo, pero es optimista
articles.standfirst: Afrontó el duelo ante el Albacete con cuatro lesionados y seis jugadores con su selección; podría recuperar alguno ante el Mallorca
articles.summary: El Girona afrontó el duelo ante el Albacete con cuatro lesionados y seis jugadores con su selección
articles.body: El Girona sobrevivió como pudo al partido contra el Albacete, que le puso contra las cuerdas y generó múltiples ocasiones de gol. Los manchegos también tenían bajas, y muchas, pero sorprendieron a un equipo blanquirrojo que no tuvo continuidad en su juego, lejos de ser dominador como lo es habitualmente ante su afición, pero que aprovechó las pocas llegadas para marcar dos tantos en el primer tiempo que dejó tocado a su rival. Quique Álvarez afrontó el duelo sin los lesionados Bryan Gil y Jastin García, a los que se les añadieron a última hora Stuani, con una lesión muscular, y Fran Beltrán, que notó un pinchazo y no quiso forzar para intentar recuperarse a tiempo para el próximo partido, también en Montilivi, contra el Mallorca, otro favorito al ascenso directo. Además de los cuatro lesionados, tampoco estaban Holmes Junior, Asprilla, Lass, Vanat, Pyshchur y Krapyvtsov, los seis jugadores repartidos por el mundo con sus selecciones. Tremendo. No contar con diez futbolistas trastoca los planes de cualquier conjunto, y más cuando cinco de ellos son titulares indiscutibles para el técnico (Junior, Fran Beltrán, Bryan Gil, Asprilla y Vanat), que viene tapando agujeros en ataque con un Van de Beek que, por suerte, va respondiendo. También dio la alternativa como titular a Javi Sarasa del filial, quien no defraudó con minutos de gran nivel. E hizo debutar a dos de las nuevas caras, todavía sin minutos hasta entonces, como Mateu Morey y Unai Hernández, poco a poco a su mejor nivel físico. El club blanquirrojo trabaja para poder contar contra el Mallorca con Holmes Junior después de jugar, o quedar liberado, del cuarto partido programado de la selección española Sub 18, que está jugando la UEFA Friendly Cup en Nyon. A España le queda jugar un tercer encuentro el 30 de septiembre contra Canadá y un cuarto con rival todavía por definir el 3 de octubre. También podría tener disponibles a partir del próximo viernes a Lass, ya sin más compromisos con Guinea, y los ucranianos sub 21 Pyshchur y Krapyvtsov. Pero todo está en el aire.

articles.title: Manchester City charges: Everything we know so far about Premier League allegations and what happens from here
articles.summary: Why has Premier League not commented on reports it has found Manchester City guilty in majority of alleged charges case? When will we hear official judgement? How serious is Friday's leak and why couldn't Man City take their case to the Court of Arbitration in Sport?
articles.body:
Reports last Friday said an independent tribunal has reached decisions in the case between the league and the club, and Sky Sports News understands the process is moving to the appeal stage.

Here's the latest on developments since, which have included Man City chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak penning an open letter to the club's fans and chief executive Ferran Soriano saying the case could take years to conclude.

Why has the Premier League not commented?

Because it's a private and confidential process.

I've heard people criticise the Premier League for not issuing a statement, but their hands are tied behind their back.

They have to respect the process, which says that everything has to be private and confidential.

That's the reason why Premier League CEO Richard Masters has given nothing away when he has been asked about this subject. He's always said there isn't much he can say, he just has to let the process play out.

When can we expect to hear an official judgement?

What we got on Friday was a leak. It's been widely reported that Man City have lost the majority of the 115 charges they faced, but there has been no official confirmation that this is the case.

The two parties involved, the Premier League and Man City, both have to agree for any judgement to be released.

There is no definitive answer about when the judgment will be released - we just have to be patient.

How serious is Friday's leak to the process?

I think the issue of the leak could be serious if City felt they were forced to take this all the way, for instance, to the High Court. They could argue that this process has not been fair and impartial because of what happened on Friday.

Man City have argued something like this before, in their case against UEFA they brought up the fact there had been leaks to the media.

Many well-respected sports lawyers are refusing to comment on this case at the moment because they have not seen the judgement.

The judgement will probably be hundreds of pages long, it will take a while to digest, and only then will we all be in a position where we can comment on it.

Could other clubs sue if the Premier League's charges are proven?

We're into the realm of hypotheticals but if the charges are proven, I'm sure clubs will be contacted by lawyers who want to represent them and help them seek compensation.

We've seen in the past clubs sue other clubs for compensation so it is something that could happen but you have to remember that the Premier League is made up of 20 clubs.

Going forward, those 20 members have to think about the Premier League as a whole as well, so we have to wait and see how much appetite there is to take legal action against Manchester City if that possibility arises in the future.

Man City previously took UEFA to the Court of Arbitration for Sport to appeal. Why couldn't that happen here?

The Premier League regulations don't include the possibility of being able to go to the Court of Arbitration for Sport. The rules are very clear. There is an independent tribunal. After the judgement of the independent tribunal, both sides can go to an appeal board.

The appeal would be heard by a new three-person panel. After that you effectively reach the end of the road because you can't go to CAS.

Having said that, if you have some serious issues with the way the process was conducted, then you do have the option, for instance, of going to the High Court and arguing it was unfair.

What did former City boss Roberto Mancini talk about on Sunday?

This is all to do with an allegation published by German outlet Der Spiegel in 2018. They said they had documents which they claimed showed that when Roberto Mancini was the Man City manager, he had two contracts.

These emails apparently alleged that Mancini was being paid £1.45m net to be the manager of Man City, while at the same time he also had a contract which was worth £1.75m a year to coach four days a year in Abu Dhabi at a club called Al Jazira.

Man City have always said these emails have been taken out of context and are part of a wider effort to discredit the club.

articles.title: El Javier detrás de Aguirre
articles.standfirst: Al margen del tono distendido y socarrón, el mexicano dejó varios mensajes con carga de profundidad
articles.summary: Al margen del tono distendido y socarrón, el mexicano dejó varios mensajes con carga de profundidad
articles.body: "Dígame su nombre hijo", "Este estadio acojona", "Ustedes los de MARCA no se parecen ni en el blanco de los ojos", "Dímelo, no seas cabrón, a ver si le metí un sartenazo en la cabeza", "Imma, por favor, replantea tu pregunta" o la definitiva "me falta la pata de palo y el perico al hombro". La rueda de prensa de presentación de Javier Aguirre no defraudó. El Vasco es el vasco y si Braulio hubiera querido un funeral no le habría llamado. De hecho, el gallego, flanqueando a su gran apuesta para salvar al Valencia de la quema, no dejó de sonreír y soltó alguna carcajada durante los más de 45 minutos que duró el turno de preguntas para el entrenador. Pero al margen de la forma (radicalmente diferente y diría que necesaria), Aguirre mostró a Javier en muchas ocasiones. Mensajes de profundidad muy directos y sin matices. "No quiero hablar, quiero ganar", "No quiero a nadie a mi lado al que no le duela perder", "con esta camiseta no se puede deambular por el campo". Aquí ya hubo menos risitas. El mensaje fue duro para jugadores y club ante la detectada falta de exigencia que ha llevado al Valencia a coquetear con el descenso y que pareciera lo normal o simplemente a que todos sus equipos masculinos y femeninos estén en puestos de perder la categoría y que no pase nada. Chistecillos y buen rollo todo el que se pueda, pero en el fondo Javier fue duro con lo que ha encontrado. Habló de los lesionados y de sus caras tristes y su recuperación psicológica que ya ha empezado, de su método y de su única obsesión: "ganar". También reconoció que dinero no habrá para grandes fichajes y que la cantera (llamó a los cuatro que han debutado por su nombre), está para algo más que para hacerles una cuenta en redes sociales. El mexicano se saltó el 'juego' del objetivo. "aquí no hacen falta mensajes ni objetivos, lo que hace falta es ganar" y dejó muy claro que conocer jugadores como Copete o Mafeo no les acerca al césped. "Ni mucho menos, ya me conocerán".

articles.title: Could Erling Haaland be forced to leave Manchester City for Real Madrid, Barcelona or PSG if the club is relegated?
articles.summary: This article explores the implications for Erling Haaland's future at Manchester City in light of the club's financial charges and potential relegation. It discusses the possible impact on his contract, the interest from top European clubs like Real Madrid, Barcelona, and PSG, and what his transfer options may be if City faces severe consequences.
articles.body: Erling Haaland signed one of the longest contracts in Premier League history because he believed in Manchester City's plans for the future, but the circumstances around the club have changed dramatically since then. Reports that City have been found guilty of 114 of the 115 Premier League financial charges have brought the possibility of serious sporting sanctions back into focus, with the club expected to appeal and no punishment yet decided.But if the eventual punishment were severe enough to push City out of the Premier League, the conversation around their biggest players would change quickly. Haaland, more than almost anyone else in the squad, would become the centre of it.Haaland chose City despite knowing the 115-charge case was hanging over the clubIn January 2025, the Norwegian signed a new nine-and-a-half-year contract that runs until the summer of 2034, committing him to City for what was then described as the longest deal in Premier League history. The club confirmed the agreement and Haaland said he was happy to continue his career at the Etihad.When he was asked whether the 115 charges had influenced his decision to sign such an extraordinary contract, Haaland made clear that they had not."No, I haven't thought of that or anything," he said. "I am confident that the club know what they are doing and I really don't think I should speak too much about this."He maintained that position in March 2025 when reporters asked whether he was concerned about the possibility of a significant punishment."I don't do that, obviously, when I sign a nine-and-a-half-year contract," Haaland said. "I've said 300 times why I signed the contract. I talked to the club, got a good feeling and agreed to it in the end. That's why."By July, when he spoke to TIME, Haaland was still relying on those conversations with City's hierarchy."I spoke with the bosses, and in the end, I believe them," he said. "It's such a tricky situation for me to even sit there and speak about, because I wasn't really involved."Haaland also did not sign his new deal expecting to leave anytime soon. His contract runs until 2034, and City presented it as a long-term commitment when the extension was announced. Reports at the time also suggested that the release clauses included in his previous agreement had been removed.There have, however, been reports of a separate mechanism that could allow Haaland to leave around 2030 for a fee that would gradually decrease. So, what happens if City are actually relegated? There is reportedly no clause in Haaland’s contract that would allow him to walk away automatically if that happens. City sources have also maintained that Haaland and the club’s other key players do not have release clauses.There have, however, been reports of a separate mechanism that could allow Haaland to leave around 2030 for a fee that would gradually decrease.A heavy punishment could change the equation completelyThere’s still a long way to go before City know what punishment, if any, they will face. The reported findings are not the final word, and the club is expected to appeal. For now, that leaves the biggest question hanging over the whole situation: just how serious will the eventual punishment be?If the eventual outcome were a fine or a relatively manageable points deduction, there would be little reason to assume Haaland's position had fundamentally changed.A far more serious sporting punishment would be different.A sufficiently large points deduction could threaten City's Premier League survival, while expulsion from the division would create an even more dramatic situation. Previous reporting on the case has identified sanctions ranging from financial penalties and points deductions to more severe sporting consequences, including demotion.Money would be another big part of the equation. If City were relegated, the financial hit would be huge. The club could be forced to cut its wage bill, and Haaland’s reported £525,000-a-week ($710,000) salary would make him an obvious part of that conversation. Selling him would also bring in a massive transfer fee, making the Norwegian one of the biggest financial decisions City could face.The absence of a relegation clause means the club would still have considerable control over any transfer, and City have shown little indication that they intend to dismantle their squad simply because the legal process has reached a new stage. But if the financial and sporting consequences became severe enough, selling one of the world's most valuable players could become a very different proposition.And if Haaland himself decided that remaining outside the Premier League was not compatible with his ambitions, the situation could develop into the kind of blockbuster transfer that few clubs could afford to ignore.Real Madrid, Barcelona and PSG would be the obvious destinationsThere would be no shortage of interest if Haaland ever became available, but the combination of his wages and the transfer fee would immediately reduce the list of realistic destinations.Paris Saint-Germain would have the financial capacity to enter the conversation, while their status at the top of European football would give Haaland a route to remain in the Champions League rather than taking a step down with City.Then there are the two Spanish giants that have been linked with him for years.Barcelona president Joan Laporta is a known admirer of Haaland, and the club has previously been reported to have considered an attempt to sign the Norwegian. Barcelona's finances, however, would make a deal of this scale particularly difficult. The club has faced significant financial constraints, and finding room for Haaland's wages alongside a potentially enormous transfer fee would require considerable financial manoeuvring.There is also a footballing argument for Barcelona.Haaland would provide the specialist centre-forward presence that Barcelona have looked for at various points, while Raphinha's ability to operate from the wing or centrally could give the team some flexibility around him. Barcelona had also previously shown interest in Julian Alvarez when looking to strengthen the striker position, underlining the importance they have placed on the role.Real Madrid offer a different problem because the question would not simply be whether they can afford Haaland.Madrid have long been linked with the Norwegian, and their financial strength would make a move conceivable, but Kylian Mbappe already occupies a prominent central attacking role alongside Vinicius Junior, Jude Bellingham and the rest of the club's attacking options.Bringing Haaland into that group would therefore require a tactical reshuffle.Both Haaland and Mbappe have built their reputations as the focal points of elite attacks, so fitting them into the same team would be one of the major footballing questions surrounding any potential Madrid move. That does not make a transfer impossible, but it would make the footballing structure as important as the finances.For now, neither Barcelona nor Real Madrid has taken an official step to sign Haaland, and there is no confirmed transfer agreement involving either club.PSG have the money, while Bayern, Chelsea, Arsenal and even Leeds remain longer shotsThe financial reality means that the list cannot simply include every major European club.Bayern Munich, Chelsea and perhaps Arsenal could emerge as alternatives if Haaland were genuinely placed on the transfer market, although each would face its own financial and sporting considerations. Several Saudi Pro League clubs could also afford the wages and transfer fee, although such a move would represent a different career choice for a player still operating at the centre of European football.Then there is Leeds United, which offers the most personal storyline of all.Haaland was born in Leeds, and he grew up supporting the club where his father, Alfie Haaland, played between 1997 and 2000. A return to Yorkshire would therefore have an obvious emotional appeal and would make for one of the most striking transfers in English football.The financial reality, however, is much harder to overcome.Leeds would have to find a way to match Haaland's enormous wages as well as the transfer fee that City would demand for a player contracted until 2034. Even if the striker had a personal connection to the club, those numbers would make the move extraordinarily difficult.For now, the biggest variable is not Real Madrid, Barcelona or PSG. It is Manchester City's case itself.The reported findings have moved the long-running saga into another stage, but sanctions have not yet been settled and City are expected to appeal. Until that process produces a sporting consequence, Haaland remains a Manchester City player with a contract stretching to 2034.If the punishment ultimately leaves City in the Premier League, the transfer speculation may amount to little more than another round of headlines. If it instead threatens the club's place in English football, Haaland's future becomes one of the most significant questions in the aftermath.And even then, his contract means he would not simply walk away. articles.title: Manchester City charges: How does Cas work and why can't Man City appeal to it?
articles.summary: The Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) regulates legal disputes across the world of sport
articles.body:
Manchester City 's Premier League charges , the Africa Cup of Nations winner being overturned , and contested athlete bans at the summer and Winter Olympics - all very different sporting controversies overseen by different governing bodies, but all linked by one organisation: the Court of Arbitration for Sport (Cas).

Cas is the legal body that settles sporting disputes which require a legal resolution, with independent panels of accredited arbitrators (meaning legal experts appointed by both sides of the dispute to find a resolution) reviewing cases and reaching decisions.

Disputes can be down to governance, contractual or disciplinary issues.

More than 900 cases are filed to Cas every year, from more than 50 different sports.

Cas covers a broad range of sporting disputes, including:

elections and term rules for sports federations

recognition of national or regional sports bodies

The Cas headquarters are in Switzerland, but it can operate on-site teams for certain events.

One of the most high-profile cases involving Cas in recent years is the controversy surrounding the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations (Afcon) final.

Following a decision made by the Confederation of African Football (Caf) to overturn the result , meaning that Morocco became the winners despite being defeated by Senegal in the final, Sengal announced they would be appealing against the decision to Cas.

In July 2020, Manchester City themselves had a two-year ban from competing in European competitions overturned by Cas.

An independent panel of accredited arbitrators from Cas has been reviewing the case, with a hearing set for October.

At events like the summer and Winter Olympics, there is an on-site Cas team ready to handle all sporting disputes as quickly as possible.

For example, one of the biggest stories of the 2026 Winter Olympics emerged when Ukrainian skeleton racer Vladyslav Heraskevych was banned from competing by the International Olympic Comittee (IOC) for wearing a helmet depicting images of Ukrainian athletes killed during Russia's invasion of his country - a decision which he appealed over to Cas.

An emergency ad-hoc Cas meeting saw his case dismissed during the course of the Games.

However, many cases cannot be resolved so quickly, and can in fact take years to resolve.

For example, at the 2022 Winter Olympics, Russian's team skaters had a gold medal dropped down to bronze by the International Skating Union after skater Kamila Valieva was handed an anti-doping ban. Russia appealed to Cas, but in July 2024, had their appeal dismissed .

And US gymnast Jordan Chiles may have her 2024 Paris Olympics bronze medal reinstated as Cas continues to examine evidence that she submitted a score appeal within the legal time limits.

Why can't Manchester City appeal against their charges to Cas?

An agreement made by Premier League sides means that all cases involving the league and its clubs are conducted in England and Wales and in accordance with English law.

Cas being based in Lausanne, Switzerland means it is not permitted to get involved in cases such as the Manchester City charges.

The Premier League has its own arbitration panel which can hear cases on a narrow number of factors as the last point of contest, rather than Cas, as stated in sections W97 and X.2.4 of the Premier League's handbook.

A similar agreement is in place for clubs in the English Football League, meaning legal issues in the Championship, League One and League Two must be settled domestically.

articles.title: Lewis Ferguson on Rangers 'dream' after summer speculation about Bologna captain's future
articles.summary: The 27-year-old was linked with Rangers during the transfer window; he has played every minute in the Serie A for Bologna this season; he played for Rangers at youth level; Scotland are at home to Switzerland in the Nations League on Tuesday night
articles.body:
The 27-year-old was subject to transfer speculation after playing with Scotland in the World Cup, but he opted to remain in Italy and has played every minute and captained Bologna in every Serie A game so far, after not featuring as regularly last season.

"I was a little bit unsure but nothing was ever really that close to be honest," he said ahead of Scotland's Nations League match with Switzerland.

"I had a long think about my future and what that was going to look like and, in the end, it was still at Bologna. I've loved every moment that I've had there, so it was about continuing that journey and see where it takes me."

Ferguson, who has two years remaining on his current contract, admitted a move to Ibrox is "always in the back of my mind".

He added: "It's no secret I grew up a [Rangers] fan. That's absolutely no secret. My family is involved in the club, and it was an aspiration of mine, a dream of mine as a kid and that's not changed.

"But I don't want to speak about that while I'm still a player at Bologna. I've got too much respect for them, but in the future you never know.

"It might happen, it might not, but it's always been something in the back of my mind."

articles.title: Kovacic: "España es ahora el mejor equipo del mundo, pero no tememos a nadie"
articles.standfirst: El futbolista croata atendió a los medios antes del partido contra España.
articles.summary: El futbolista croata atendió a los medios antes del partido contra España.
articles.body: Mateo Kovacic es una de las caras conocidas de la siempre competitiva selección croata. El jugador del Manchester City, ex del Real Madrid, fue el jugador encargado de atender a los medios en la sala de prensa del Sánchez Pizjuán antes del partido frente a España. Sin contestar preguntas sobre la situación del Manchester City, pese al intento de MARCA, pero repasando el resto de la actualidad. Selección española. "Por supuesto. España, hoy por hoy, es el mejor equipo del mundo. No hay nada mejor que jugar contra los mejores" Centro del campo. "Sí, por supuesto. Es el uno de los mejores del mundo. Tienen unos jugadores espectaculares encabezados por Rodri, que es uno de los mejores del mundo". Modric. "Significa mucho para nosotros. Es una leyenda dentro y fuera del campo". El partido. "Será un partido difícil contra el mejor equipo del mundo. Pero a nosotros también. Hemos jugado varias veces contra ellos y a veces lo hemos hecho muy bien. Ojalá repetir". Su último partido. "Siempre es bueno que el seleccionador te alabe. Yo estoy aquí para justificar mi presencia, pero lo más importante es que el equipo gane". La racha de España. "Se puede interrumpir. Siempre queremos ganar, pero intentaremos hacer nuestro juego. Mañana nos espera un partido difícil, pero con un ambiente fantástico". Balón de oro. "Es muy difícil elegir. Hay muchos buenos jugadores y yo prefiero hablar del equipo. No tengo una opinión concreta". Maresca. "Es un entrenador fantástico. Lo ha demostrado. Tiene buenas ideas, buena relación con los jugadores..." España. "He disfrutado mucho viendo a España con Busquets, Xavi, Iniesta... Las dos son muy buenas. Ahora está Pedri, Yamal... Yo disfruto mucho del fútbol que juega España, pero mañana intentaremos centrarnos en nuestro juego". Lo que más teme. "No tenemos miedo a nadie. Respetamos a todos. España es muy potente como equipo. Están muy unidos. Es un equipo top, pero nos centraremos en nuestro juego". ¿Ganar es misión imposible? "No. Sabemos lo de los 39 partidos sin perder, pero no quiero ocuparme de eso, quiero ocuparme de nuestro juego y quitarles el balón".

articles.title: ‘Because of agents and family issues’: Brazil football legend Roberto Carlos reveals shocking loss of 99% of his $180m career earnings
articles.summary: Brazil football legend Roberto Carlos discloses the staggering loss of 99% of his $180 million career earnings, revealing issues with agents and family that led to his financial downfall.
articles.body: Roberto Carlos made a fortune during a 24-year career spent winning almost everything there was to win, but the former Brazil and Real Madrid star says almost all of it is now gone. The 53-year-old has revealed that he lost 99% of what he earned from football, while giving only a limited explanation of how his finances unravelled and pointing instead to serious family problems, agents and people he trusted.Carlos says people he trusted emptied his bank accountSpeaking at the Portugal Football Summit in Lisbon, Carlos opened up about his finances while discussing the importance of planning for life after football and protecting a player's image beyond the pitch."I had problems with people who emptied my bank account. I lost 99% of everything I earned from football," Carlos said.He did not provide a full breakdown of what happened to his money, but said agents and family issues were central to the financial problems he experienced."Because of agents and family issues, I lost 99% of everything I had earned in football," he added.Carlos also described the moment he realised the scale of what had happened, saying that it came with almost no warning."I had a very serious family problem. One Thursday, I went to bed at midnight and the next day, I received a pile of documents I knew nothing about. That's when I realised I had lost my entire history."Carlos did not identify the family members involved or explain precisely what the documents contained, so his comments do not establish that his children, wives or other relatives were personally responsible for the losses.His personal life has been unusually large by any measure, with Carlos having 11 children, relationships with seven women and two marriages, but he has not publicly attributed the financial problems to any particular member of his family.Reports from Globo have also pointed to problems involving agents and advisers, although Carlos himself has remained relatively vague about the precise circumstances.The numbers involved make the admission particularly striking. Estimates put Carlos' career football earnings at around $180 million, meaning that losing 99% would amount to more than $178 million and leave roughly $1.8 million from that original sum.Celebrity Net Worth, meanwhile, currently estimates his net worth at $5 million, although that figure is separate from Carlos' own account of losing 99% of his football earnings.His playing career generated enormous wealthCarlos had the kind of career that made significant wealth possible, particularly during the peak years of European football's spending boom.He spent 11 seasons with Real Madrid, making 527 appearances and winning four La Liga titles and three Champions League trophies. He played alongside Zinedine Zidane, Luis Figo, Ronaldo and David Beckham during the club's famous Galácticos era and became one of the defining left-backs of his generation.When Carlos renewed his Real Madrid contract in 2000, he reportedly received an $8.5 million signing bonus alongside a $5.1 million annual salary, with the club also covering his home rent and six trips to São Paulo each season.After leaving Madrid in 2007, he joined Fenerbahçe, where he earned €4.2 million net per season.Even later in his career, the money remained substantial. In 2011, at the age of 37, Russian club Anzhi Makhachkala offered him a contract worth €6 million per year, then approximately $9 million.Carlos eventually continued playing into his 40s, making his final appearances as a player-manager in India in 2015.Across those years, his football career is estimated to have generated around $180 million, a figure that reflects both his club contracts and the extraordinary commercial value attached to one of the sport's most recognisable defenders.The career behind the fortune was extraordinaryCarlos' financial story is difficult to separate from just how successful he was as a footballer.For Brazil, he played at three World Cups and helped the country win the 2002 tournament after reaching the final four years earlier. He made more than 120 appearances for the national team and spent much of his peak being regarded as not only the world's leading left-back but one of the best players in football.He came close to major individual honours as well. Carlos finished second to Ronaldo in the 1997 FIFA World Player of the Year voting and again finished second to his Brazilian teammate for the 2002 Ballon d'Or after winning the World Cup.His most famous moment may have come in 1997, when his free-kick against France appeared to be travelling several yards wide before swerving dramatically back towards the goal. The strike became one of football's most famous goals and was subsequently studied by physicists because of the unusual trajectory.Away from the pitch, Carlos says he had always understood that his playing career would eventually end and that he needed something to fall back on."I made mistakes, and therefore, I ask younger players not to do the same. I always thought about future plans after my playing career," he said.Carlos said he had already obtained his sporting director's licence by the time he decided to leave football and was working with several brands, allowing him to build a second career around his name and reputation."It's about building a history as a player and leveraging your image," he said. "When I decided to leave football, I already had my sporting director's licence and was working with many brands."Carlos now works in football and continues to operate as a brand ambassador, including in his role with Real Madrid as an ambassador for Asia and Oceania and director of institutional relations.His warning to younger players is consequently less about the size of a footballer's salary than what happens around it. Carlos earned millions at some of the biggest clubs in the world, built a career that produced World Cup and Champions League titles, and became one of the most recognisable players of his era.Yet he says that people he trusted, agents and serious family problems ultimately left him with only a fraction of what that career had generated.Carlos has not provided all the details behind the losses, but his message at the Portugal Football Summit was clear enough: earning a fortune during a football career is one thing, protecting it when other people have access to your finances is another.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: El Atlético más internacional... ¡supera a Madrid y Barça!
articles.standfirst: Con Le Normand son 17 los jugadores que están con sus selecciones. Barrios y Sorloth, ahora lesionados, son habituales con sus combinados nacionales
articles.summary: Con Le Normand son 17 los jugadores que están con sus selecciones. Barrios y Sorloth, ahora lesionados, son habituales con sus combinados nacionales
articles.body: El nuevo, por duración, parón FIFA de tres semanas ha causado estragos en los grandes equipos de Europa. En lo que respecta a LaLiga, los tres grandes han sido los más perjudicados como es lógico por el potencial de sus plantillas. Así, hace una semana el balance de jugadores con sus selecciones lo lideraba el Barcelona, con 17. Atlético y Real Madrid completaban el podio con 16 y 15 futbolistas con sus respectivas selecciones nacionales. En clave rojiblanca, el sorpasso ha llegado tras la disputa del primer encuentro de La Roja. Eric García se lesionó (curiosamente fue reemplazado por un rojiblanco, Marc Pubill, en el lateral derecho) y dejó la expedición de la actual campeona del mundo. Su sustituto, otro jugador del Atlético, un Le Normand que convierte a los del Metropolitano en el equipo más internacional. 17 jugadores están con sus selecciones y apenas cinco (Llorente, que se ha retirado de la selección de forma voluntaria, Koke, Arnau, Dani Martínez y Cardoso) volverán mañana a los entrenamientos a las órdenes de Simeone. El número de internacionales se aumentaría de no ser por las lesiones de Sorloth y Barrios. El noruego es fijo con su selección, mientras que el canterano se estaba haciendo un hueco entre los elegidos por De la Fuente cuando las lesiones le empezaron a golpear... hasta quedarse sin el Mundial que culminó a toda una generación.

articles.title: Bilic: "España tiene cositas que podemos aprovechar"
articles.standfirst: Rueda de prensa del seleccionador croata antes del España-Croacia
articles.summary: Rueda de prensa del seleccionador croata antes del España-Croacia
articles.body: Slaven Bilic, seleccionador croata, acaba de pasar por la sala de prensa del Sánchez-Pizjuán para analizar el duelo de mañana ante España. Su regreso a la selección croata, la que comandó entre 2006 y 2012, fue con una victoria contra la República Checa en Praga. Eso hace que mañana se enfrente los dos equipos que comandan el grupo después de los primeros 90 minutos de juego. Victoria en Praga: "Entiendo las críticas. Vi conclusiones que no tienen que ver con la verdad. No llevar la mano al corazón en los himnos fue un error. Respeto lo que se dice. Pido perdón, ya está olvidado". Puerta cerrada: "No está bien tener que jugar sin público. Echaremos de menos a nuestra gente. Es una gran pena. Ese partido ante Inglaterra es una gran fiesta. Ningún partido de ese nivel se debería jugar sin gente". Modric y Rodri: "Son dos ganadores del Balón de Oro. Bielsa dijo que Luka es un 6, un 8 y un 10. Así que es un 24. Rodri es el mejor 6 del mundo. No se trata de elegir, porque pueden jugar juntos". Cambios: "Tenemos cantidad y calidad. Nos importa la Liga de las Naciones, pero es también un proceso hacia la Euro. No digo qué equipo jugará, porque nadie lo hace. Tenemos jugadores cansados otros algo enfermos. Veremos". España: "Son los mejores del mundo.No se van a relajar, nosotros tampoco. España tiene cositas que se pueden aprovechar, lo demostró Inglaterra. No necesitamos un milagro, necesitamos fe. Hemos jugado grandes partidos contra ellos. Los partidos son largos. Contra los checios hubo momentos en los que no supimos sufrir. No se puede repetir. Sabemos que la posesión será para ellos, pero no puede ser siempre de ellos. En 2012 pudimos eliminar a España. Debemos tener confianza en lo que hacemos, en nosotros". 2010, 2012, ahora y Lamine: "El fútbol cambia. La de 2012 tenía más toque, no tenía la velocidad de ahora de Lamine Yamal. Sus transiciones no eran tan veloces. Con eso ya digo todo lo que pienso de Lamine".

articles.title: Lewis Ferguson: Rangers dream remains but Bologna exit 'was never close'
articles.summary: Lewis Ferguson reveals "nothing was ever that close" on a move away from Bologna this summer amid reports of interest from Rangers but he does harbour ambitions of a return to his boyhood club.
articles.body:
Lewis Ferguson says he was never close to leaving Bologna this summer amid reports of interest from boyhood club Rangers.

But the Scotland midfielder, 27, does retain aspirations of an Ibrox return at some stage in his career.

Ferguson was released by Rangers at 14 and made his way to Serie A in 2022, via Hamilton Academical and Aberdeen.

He has captained Bologna since 2023 and led them to their first Coppa Italia in over 50 years in 2025.

However, starts became sparse last term under Vincenzo Italiano, making just 17 in the league.

Asked about links to Rangers, Ferguson said: "I had a long think after the World Cup about my future and I was a little bit unsure but nothing was ever that close."

Pocognoli has no concern over Scotland's lack of goals

From shaky start to statement wins - 100 days of McInnes at Rangers

And he added: "When I went back for pre-season, we had a new manager [Domenico Tedesco] and it was like a fresh start.

"We changed again since [with Raffaele Palladino], so I've had three new managers in the last two months [including Sebastien Pocognoli with Scotland].

"I had a long think about what my future was going to look like and in the end it was still at Bologna.

"I've loved every moment that I've had there. It was just about continuing that journey and seeing where it takes me."

Ferguson, who is under contract until 2028 with the option of a further year, has played every minute of Bologna's five Serie A games so far this season.

His father, Derek, and uncle, Barry, both played for Rangers with the latter captaining and at one stage managing at Ibrox.

In July, newly-installed Rangers manager Derek McInnes spoke of an "obvious link" with Ferguson, having worked with the player at Aberdeen.

On his bond with Rangers, Ferguson said: "It's no secret that I grew up a fan and my family is involved in the club.

"It was a dream of mine as a kid and that's not changed but I don't want to speak about that while I'm a player at Bologna.

"In the future, you never know. It might happen, it might not, but it's always been something in the back of mind."

articles.title: El salto que le falta al fútbol español
articles.standfirst: Pese a ser primera en el ránking FIFA, los ingresos de la RFEF por la equipación son cinco veces menores que Francia, Alemania o Brasil… ¡¡¡e incluso están por debajo de Portugal e Italia!!!
articles.summary: Pese a ser primera en el ránking FIFA, los ingresos de la RFEF por la equipación son cinco veces menores que Francia, Alemania o Brasil… ¡¡¡e incluso están por debajo de Portugal e Italia!!!
articles.body: La Selección vive su momento más dulce en el campo y en la calle, pero sus ingresos por equipación siguen bastante lejos de los de Francia, Alemania o Brasil. Acercarse a los 100 millones que cobran estas selecciones parece cuestión de justicia. Basta asomarse a una sesión a puerta abierta en la Ciudad del Fútbol de Las Rozas para entenderlo. Hay padres con la camiseta de 2010, niños con el dorsal de sus nuevos ídolos recién estampado y abuelos que no se perdieron ni un partido del Mundial de Estados Unidos. La segunda estrella, que se estrenó en Wembley y lucirá oficialmente por primera vez en nuestro país este martes 29 en Sevilla, ha desatado algo que va más allá de una celebración. España se ha enamorado otra vez de su Selección, y esta vez parece que va para largo. Ese furor se nota en las gradas de Las Rozas, en los aeropuertos, en los hoteles de concentración y en cada ciudad por la que pasa el equipo. La Real Federación Española de Fútbol lo sabe y ha decidido aprovecharlo. Su objetivo es tan ambicioso como claro: quintuplicar los ingresos que genera la marca de sus equipaciones. España debería estar en el podio de las federaciones que más ingresan por su equipación, y los motivos son el rendimiento deportivo, la trayectoria reciente y un futuro que apunta muy alto. Los números hablan solos. España es número 1 del ranking FIFA en categoría masculina y también en femenina, algo al alcance de muy pocos. Las categorías inferiores también compiten por todos los títulos, los ganan (sin ir más lejos: el reciente campeonato del mundo obtenido por la selección femenina sub20) y siguen sacando talento que acaba en los mejores clubes de Europa. Además, en el horizonte está el Mundial de 2030, que España organizará junto a Portugal y Marruecos. Será un escaparate global como no se ha visto en décadas. Con todo eso, la conclusión en Las Rozas es clara: España tiene que codearse en caché con quienes hoy lideran este mercado. Si la Federación tiene argumentos para sentarse a negociar, muchos llevan nombre y apellido. Pocas selecciones del mundo reúnen a la vez a tantos jugadores con repercusión planetaria, y casi ninguna los tiene tan jóvenes. Y, además, con tan elevado valor de mercado. Lamine Yamal es el gran reclamo, como indiscutible icono planetario, a pesar de su bisoñez. Su camiseta se vende en todos los continentes y cada regate suyo se convierte en tendencia en las redes. Detrás del fenómeno hay jugadores que sostienen el equipo, como Pau Cubarsí, que juega con una madurez impropia de su edad, y Nico Williams, pura electricidad por la banda e ídolo de los más pequeños. En el equipo femenino la historia es la misma. Vicky López es la cabeza visible de una generación que ha convertido a España en la referencia del fútbol femenino y ya acumula galardones individuales. Detrás de ella llega Clara Serrajordi, uno de los talentos más prometedores de Europa y la prueba de que la cantera no se agota. Para una marca deportiva, esto vale oro. No son estrellas en el final de su carrera. Son futbolistas que llegarán al Mundial de 2030 en plenitud y que marcarán el fútbol de la próxima década. Quien vista a España vestirá a varios de los jugadores más seguidos del planeta, tanto en el equipo masculino como en el femenino. Es un activo que ni Francia, ni Alemania, ni Brasil pueden ofrecer ahora mismo con esa combinación de juventud, títulos y proyección. Arriba del todo están Francia, Alemania y Brasil. Las tres federaciones ingresan cerca de 100 millones de euros por temporada gracias a sus contratos de equipación, y alguna incluso supera esa cifra. El caso de Alemania es significativo, pues ha renegociado al alza el valor de su elástica rompiendo un vínculo histórico con Adidas y yéndose con su archirrival Nike. Hoy la distancia es grande. Si la meta es multiplicar por cinco los ingresos actuales, queda claro lo lejos que está el valor comercial de la camiseta roja de su valor deportivo. España gana, emociona y vende, pero cobra como una selección de segunda fila. La RFEF necesita jugar mejor ese partido. Otro dato que chirría es que Italia y Portugal aparecen por delante de España en esta clasificación. El caso italiano es especialmente llamativo. La Azzurra no ha jugado ninguno de los tres últimos Mundiales y, aun así, su camiseta cotiza más que la de España. Portugal tiene el tirón global de sus estrellas, pero su palmarés reciente no se puede comparar con el español. La paradoja deja clara una cosa: el mercado de las equipaciones premia la historia y el marketing acumulado durante años, no solo el rendimiento del momento. La Federación quiere corregir precisamente ese desfase. El movimiento tiene nombre propio. Adidas es el socio actual e histórico de la Selección y partirá con ventaja. Las principales marcas del mercado siguen de cerca todos los movimientos y el desembarco de alguna otra casa comercial, como la que ha fichado a Kylian Mbappé, puede mover también este apasionante tablero. Desde la Federación siempre han pregonado su cercanía, que viene de lejos, con adidas. Sin embargo, es una obviedad que el fútbol español tiene que dar un gran salto en este capítulo. la Selección debe seguir siendo puntera y vestir a Lamine Yamal, Vicky López, Cubarsí, Nico Williams o Serrajordi debe tener un precio acorde a lo que representan. El contrato actual vence en 2030, justo el año del Mundial en casa. Sin embargo, la renegociación suele arrancar con el inicio del nuevo ciclo mundialista. Esperar a 2030 sería perder cuatro años de un momento que no se repite con frecuencia. España ha ganado en el campo todo lo que se podía ganar. En la grada ha recuperado a una generación entera de aficionados y ha conquistado a otra nueva, la de los niños que hoy llenan Las Rozas con el nombre de Lamine o de Vicky a la espalda. Queda una asignatura pendiente: que el valor de su camiseta esté a la altura de lo que representa. No estar entra las cinco mejor pagadas por sus equipaciones resultaría una anomalía histórica.

articles.title: Bernard Somuah pasa por quirófano y estará cuatro meses de baja
articles.standfirst: Se lesionó del tobillo en el encuentro ante el Almería
articles.summary: Se lesionó del tobillo en el encuentro ante el Almería
articles.body: Bernard Somuah fue operado en la mañana de este lunes. Según informa el club, ‘la intervención quirúrgica transcurrió de manera satisfactoria y según lo previsto’. El delantero ghanés del Celta Fortuna estará de baja durante cuatro meses por sufrir una rotura de la sindesmosis del tobillo izquierdo que se produjo hace diez días ante la UD Almería tras un giro brusco en una desafortunada acción, al borde del descanso. El entrenador Fredi Álvarez le desea una pronta recuperación: “Para nosotros es un jugador importante porque es incómodo para las defensas rivales. Lo perdemos, pero lo peor es para él, es el primer perjudicado, ojalá pronto se recupere, se recupere bien y ojalá podamos contar con él cuanto antes”. La plantilla ayudará en el proceso al futbolista, según afirma el técnico: “Un jugador que sale de su casa, que está lejos de su familia y ahora tiene que vivir una situación como esta y no es fácil y vamos tener que ayudarle en el día a día".

articles.title: Senate Nears Vote on College Sports Bill That Would Rein in Athlete Payments and Transfers
articles.summary: WASHINGTON (AP) — The Senate is poised to pass a sweeping bipartisan bill on Monday that would regulate college sports, an attempt to end "chaos" in an industry that has been upended by skyrocketing athlete payments and near-unrestricted transfers between schools.
articles.body:
WASHINGTON (AP) — The Senate is poised to pass a sweeping bipartisan bill on Monday that would regulate college sports , an attempt to end "chaos" in an industry that has been upended by skyrocketing athlete payments and near-unrestricted transfers between schools.

Passage of the legislation would be the strongest effort yet by Congress to set national regulations governing payments to college athletes for their name, image and likeness and how often they can transfer. It would give the NCAA new authority over those rules and limited antitrust protections to enforce them.

The bill is the product of years of Senate negotiations that intensified as some in the industry pleaded with Congress to step in after a 2025 lawsuit settlement uprooted the college sports landscape by allowing colleges to pay their players. The legislation, which would still have to pass the House, would codify the settlement into law but also establish new guardrails around the system in an attempt to rein in the runaway costs for colleges.

"It would be nice if college sports could somehow magically fix itself, but this is a matter of law, federal law, and only Congress can fix it," said Senate Commerce Committee Chairman Ted Cruz, R-Texas, who negotiated the bill with the top Democrat on the panel, Washington Sen. Maria Cantwell.

The bill's backers — more than 70 senators from both parties — say it aims to curtail constant litigation and uncertainty across college sports for athletes, schools and fans. It would also give hundreds of thousands of student athletes new health and labor protections.

Critics say the bill doesn't do enough to protect athletes or curtail the enormous sums of money flowing to coaches, colleges and conferences.

"This is a bill that essentially ensconces a system of exploitation, and it doesn't fix the broader problems," said Connecticut Sen. Chris Murphy, a Democrat who has worked with labor and civil rights groups to rally opposition to the bill.

President Donald Trump has repeatedly expressed an interest in the legislation , and the White House formally endorsed the bill last month. But it could face an uphill battle in the House, which failed repeatedly over the last year to get a different version to the floor and is in recess until after the November elections.

Lawmakers will have to start over in the next Congress if the bill doesn't pass both chambers by the end of the year.

Bill addresses skyrocketing spending, unlimited transfers

College sports have been reeling in the wake of the 2025 court settlement allowing colleges to directly pay players for their name, image and likeness. The fallout has reshaped the industry and led to football roster payrolls that can exceed $40 million .

The bill codifies the court settlement, including a revenue cap that allows schools to share up to $21.5 million in revenue with their players. The legislation would more than double that amount for some schools, allowing up to an additional $27.5 million in payments through a retention fund , and would give schools and conferences the option of pooling their TV media rights to potentially raise more revenue.

The legislation also aims to stabilize the NCAA transfer portal that has led to players constantly switching teams. It would restrict player transfers to one "free" move over five years without sitting out a year, with some exceptions, and also restricts players to five years of total eligibility.

The proposed eligibility limit comes amid backlash to schools that have increasingly pushed boundaries, including LSU's now-canceled plans to place players on the roster who had participated in NFL training camps.

"That was probably like a big lamp for some people who saw it and said, 'Oh my God, this is so out of control,'" Cantwell said in a recent interview with The Associated Press. "You can see how out-of-hand the situation was getting."

The bill also would restrict coaches from leaving their schools during the season and prevent conferences from growing larger than 19 programs, an effort to prevent so-called "superleagues" from taking over sports. It would force schools that want to switch conferences to spend three years as an independent — down from five years in the original bill. That change brought new supporters on board, including Florida State and Clemson of the Atlantic Coast Conference.

Critics say it wouldn't do enough to help athletes

The legislation includes new protections for athletes, including caps on agent fees and guarantees for health insurance and certain scholarships. It would also require schools to maintain a minimum number of sports and roster spots — an effort to ensure that women's and Olympic sports are not cut in favor of football, basketball and other sports that generate more revenue.

Still, some Democrats say it wouldn't do enough to limit the big money in college sports.

The legislation "places a cap on the students' cut of the revenues, but there are no caps on coaches' salaries or on the size of donations to athletic programs," Murphy said last week.

Virginia Sen. Tim Kaine said that the new antitrust protections would make it harder for athletes to sue universities, and "taking away their legal rights strikes me as a bridge too far."

Groups like the NAACP, Congressional Black Caucus and AFL-CIO have also opposed the bill, in part, because it leaves unresolved whether athletes should be considered employees with the ability to collectively bargain.

All four Black Democrats in the Senate — Sens. Cory Booker of New Jersey, Raphael Warnock of Georgia, Lisa Blunt Rochester of Delaware and Angela Alsobrooks of Maryland — have opposed the bill.

Booker, who played football at Stanford in the late 1980s on a scholarship, said in a Senate floor speech earlier this month that he was "afforded opportunities I never would have had if it wasn't for college athletics" but that he also "saw how unjust the NCAA is."

He said it wasn't until college athletes were able to begin to win cases in court that the power started to shift, "and now the NCAA is coming here to the United States Senate, asking for sweeping powers" to exempt antitrust laws.

Some Republicans also said it is overreach.

The legislation "goes way too far inserting the federal government into collegiate athletics," said Republican Sen. Rick Scott of Florida, who is opposing it.

Despite strong bipartisan support in the Senate, the bill faces a murky path in the House.

House lawmakers won't return to Washington until mid-November, after the elections. And it's unclear what will be on Republican leaders' agenda in the chaotic last few weeks of the session.

Pressure from Trump could help push the bill to passage. But some House Republicans have insisted on language explicitly stating that athletes are not employees, which the Senate bill does not have — a key concession to Cantwell to win enough Democratic support.

House Education and Workforce Committee Chairman Tim Walberg, R-Mich., and House Energy and Commerce Chairman Brett Guthrie, R-Ky., said in a statement in May that "any lasting framework must confront the central issue that continues to cast uncertainty over the future of college sports: whether student-athletes will ultimately be treated as employees."

"Congress cannot deliver real stability, consistency, or certainty to schools, conferences, and student-athletes while leaving that question unresolved," the two Republicans said.

articles.title: El Málaga encuentra en Pablo Martínez a su lanzador
articles.standfirst: El ex del Levante se ha hecho dueño del balón parado
articles.summary: El ex del Levante se ha hecho dueño del balón parado
articles.body: El Málaga vuelve a tener especialista a balón parado. Después de unos años en los que nadie se había atrevido a coger las riendas de las faltas laterales y los saques de esquina, los de Juanfran Funes han encontrado en Pablo Martínez una figura importante en ese aspecto. El Málaga encontró en el ex del Levante algo más que un centrocampista con experiencia y jerarquía. El madrileño, uno de los refuerzos del conjunto blanquiazul este verano, llega a La Rosaleda con una cualidad que puede adquirir especial importancia durante la temporada: su buen golpeo a balón parado. El propio club ha destacado en estas semanas de competición en su perfil de la web su capacidad en esta faceta, tanto en lanzamientos de falta como en los saques de esquina. El balón parado no es un recurso menor para un Málaga que está teniendo dificultades para generar peligro en ataque. Las acciones a balón parado pueden convertirse en una alternativa para un equipo que necesita encontrar nuevas vías hacia el gol y, en ese escenario, la llegada de Martínez ofrece una posibilidad diferente. Su capacidad para poner buenos centros y su golpeo pueden permitir a Funes contar con un nuevo especialista en faltas laterales, córners e incluso acciones directas. En Vigo se pudo ver el pie de Pablo Martínez, que empezó a destacar en este aspecto en el Santiago Bernabéu. Funes le ha elegido como el lanzador y de momento el madrileño ha respondido con una asistencia de gol. Pablo Martínez ya dejó muestras de ello durante su etapa en el Levante, donde se convirtió en una pieza importante y llegó a ejercer como capitán. El centrocampista acumula 155 partidos oficiales con el conjunto granota, además de experiencia en Primera y Segunda División. Ahora, en su primera temporada como malaguista, ha disputado cinco encuentros en sus 307 minutos sobre el césped.

articles.summary: El actual director deportivo del Espanyol ejerce como padrino de la V Edición de la Reyes Cup
articles.body: Este lunes se ha presentado la V Edición de la Reyes Cup, el evento que cada año quiere recordar y rendir homenaje a la figura de José Antonio Reyes. Organizado por la Hermandad de Muchachos de Consolación de Utrera, el Ayuntamiento de la localidad y la Junta de Andalucía, este torneo de fútbol base reunirá categorías alevín, benjamín y bebé tanto masculina como femenina y se celebrará entre los días 9 y 11 de octubre en el Estadio San Juan Bosco. El padrino de esta nueva edición será Monchi, que atendió a los medios durante su presentación. "Es remover un poquito los recuerdos, evidentemente, y acordarnos de muchas cosas. Cuando estaba viendo el vídeo de presentación del torneo, pues te acuerdas de muchos momentos que vienen rápidamente del pasado al presente y te traen una sonrisa dentro de lo que se le echa de menos y de lo difícil que es todavía su ausencia. Pero creo que actividades, actuaciones, torneos como este, hacen que todos lo volvamos a recordar y que busquemos siempre la parte más bonita y más emotiva de José Antonio", empezó el actual director deportivo del Espanyol. Talento natural: "Talento cada vez sale más, talento natural cada vez menos. La Ciudad Deportiva de Sevilla ha dado mucho talento: Sergio, Jesús, Marchena, Jesuli, Salva, Velasco… mucho, pero como José Antonio, natural ninguno. Actualmente la formación cada vez es más pronta, más temprana, entonces, el talento surge a través del trabajo. Pero talento como José Antonio, que no hace falta trabajarlo, es muy difícil encontrarlo porque era muy innato". Recuerdos: "Tengo muchos recuerdos buenos con José Antonio, también alguna bronca porque con él tenía una relación muy cercana desde que era un niño, su familia igual. Me quedo con muchos momentos. Ese pase en Varsovia a Carlos Bacca, en esa cuarta Europa League contra el Dnipro, posiblemente es la foto más bonita. También me acuerdo de esos derbis en los que él era extraordinario, cómo era capaz de dar la vuelta a su forma de enfocar los partidos, porque para él un derbi era algo muy señalado. Hay muchos momentos muy bonitos con José". Trofeo Antonio Puerta: "El viernes es para mí un partido especial, no solamente por Antonio, sino porque juegan dos equipos con los que he trabajado, Sevilla y Aston Villa. Va a ser también muy bonito, creo que es un homenaje también muy merecido para Antonio". Etapa con el Espanyol: "Contento, me han acogido de una manera extraordinaria, trabajando muy a gusto, con gente muy cercana con la que ya había trabajado como Fernando o Miguel Ángel, muy cercana a la propiedad. Barcelona es una ciudad muy bonita, espectacular, y me permiten venir para darle tiempo también al Club Deportivo San Fernando, que también era uno de los objetivos de este año. A día de hoy, satisfecho con cómo me estoy encontrando. Con ganas de tener algunos puntos más, que nos faltan, pero bien en general". Actual Sevilla: "Creo que ha encontrado una buena línea de rendimiento y resultados. Es para que los seguidores estén satisfechos y contentos. Han tenido solo dos derrotas contra dos equipos muy complicados, el Atlético de Madrid y el Barcelona, el empate contra nosotros y el resto son victorias, con lo cual creo que es para que aficionados, club, técnicos y jugadores estén contentos". José Ignacio Navarro: "Yo lo conozco de hace muchos años. Tuve el gusto de ser trabajador con él al principio, en los inicios, y me alegro. Creo que la gente que es trabajadora merece que las cosas le salgan bien, y José Ignacio es un tipo muy trabajador". Balón de Oro: "Es complicado. Hay una terna o cuatro jugadores que pueden optar a ello. Si tiro por ser español creo que lo merecería Lamine. Pero también imagino que los franceses pensarán que lo merece Mbappé y los ingleses a lo mejor Harry Kane. Siempre va a despertar controversias".

articles.title: Cape Verde World Cup hero Vozinha has 28m followers, new club and Ballon d’Or nomination but now wants his old life back
articles.summary: Vozinha, the Cape Verdean goalkeeper who shot to fame after an incredible World Cup performance, reflects on his newfound celebrity status and longing for his old life, amidst career advancements and overwhelming attention from fans and brands.
articles.body: Six months ago, Vozinha was a goalkeeper playing in Portugal's second tier, living quietly in the small city of Chaves with little attention beyond Cape Verde. Then came seven saves against Spain at the World Cup, a million Instagram followers in a day and a level of fame he never expected. Now, with more than 28 million followers, he says he would choose his old life back.Seven saves against Spain changed Vozinha's lifeFor anyone who follows football, Vozinha is now one of the recognisable faces of Cape Verde's remarkable World Cup story. Before the tournament, however, the 40-year-old goalkeeper was largely unknown outside his country and the Portuguese football circuit, where his professional life was centred on the small city of Chaves and the second tier.His real name is Josimar Jose Evora Dias, but it was the name Vozinha that suddenly became familiar around the world after Cape Verde's opening group match against Spain.The goalkeeper produced seven saves and kept a clean sheet against the side that would eventually become world champions, turning what had been an ordinary international fixture into the performance that transformed his life. Before kick-off, his Instagram account had around 56,000 followers. Within 24 hours, that number had passed one million.The explosion began with CazéTV, the Brazilian broadcaster that held rights to the tournament, encouraging its audience to follow Vozinha during the historic goalless draw.He did not initially understand what was happening.“A member of the team’s catering staff came up to me and told me I had a billion followers,” Vozinha told The Observer. “I had no idea what he was talking about; I thought he was joking, but he insisted. Later, I went to do some interviews in the mixed zone and a CazéTV journalist asked me if I knew what was happening.”The journalist showed him her phone, and that was when Vozinha saw that more than one million people were suddenly following his account.“She showed me her phone and that was when I saw that I had more than a million followers. I decided to turn off my Instagram notifications so I wouldn’t be tempted to keep checking who was following me.”The number did not stop there. Vozinha now has more than 28 million Instagram followers, putting him ahead of prominent American sports figures including Travis Kelce, Patrick Mahomes and Tom Brady.The attention became so overwhelming that Vozinha, together with the Cape Verdean Football Federation, brought back his former manager to help deal with the sudden noise surrounding him and the team. Someone close to the dressing room told The Observer: “It wasn’t easy to get back to normal.”Even with his notifications switched off, friends continued telling him which famous people had started following him, while companies and brands began approaching him with commercial opportunities.“I know that during the World Cup there were lots of companies and brands that wanted to work with me,” Vozinha said, “but while we were competing I only did one promotional collaboration, with UFL Mobile. I don’t know what offers might come in the future, but for now I don’t want to work with any tobacco, alcohol or betting brands.”The fame followed him away from the football pitchThe World Cup gave Vozinha a new professional profile, but it also changed the most ordinary parts of his life.Speaking to The Observer, he explained that going out for dinner or simply being in public now comes with a level of attention he never experienced before.“I’ve lost my peace and tranquillity,” he said. “I no longer have any privacy, or at least much less than I used to. Now I go out, I go to a restaurant, and there’s always someone who wants to take a photo with me or asks me for an autograph. Or, worse, someone is filming me.“That’s what has changed most in my life, and I don’t think there’s anything I can do about it.”The attention has also reached his family in Cape Verde.His mother, who Vozinha describes as someone who finds it difficult to say no to people, now has supporters arriving at her home almost every day asking for photographs or wanting to speak with her. His father, who is more reserved, has learned to keep his distance.“I’m not there, so I can’t help them,” Vozinha said. “They have to learn to live with the situation and set boundaries.”That loss of privacy has made the goalkeeper unusually candid about the less attractive side of becoming famous, particularly because fame was never something he appears to have been seeking.“A lot of people want to be famous and have a public profile, but they only see the positive side of that reality,” Vozinha said. “To be honest, if I were offered the life I have today or the life I had before, I’d choose the one I had before.”For all the attention surrounding him, Vozinha has also been careful not to turn Cape Verde's World Cup into an individual achievement.The country went unbeaten in Group H, reached the knockout stage and produced one of the tournament's most unexpected stories. Vozinha was the standout performer, keeping two clean sheets and making 18 saves across the tournament before Cape Verde eventually lost 3-2 to Argentina after a late own goal from Diney Borges.“It’s nice to feel like a kind of ambassador, but I want to make it clear that what we achieved was a collective effort,” Vozinha said.“We made history and the best news would be if we could harness that momentum to develop our country and improve the living conditions of our people.”His World Cup turned into a new careerThe attention around Vozinha did not disappear when Cape Verde's tournament ended.His performances helped earn him a move to Colo-Colo, the biggest and most successful football club in Chile, after the club showed the strongest interest in signing him.“They were the club that showed the most interest,” Vozinha said. “I didn’t receive any offers from the United States and there was some contact with Saudi Arabia, but nothing concrete. Hopefully I can play in the Copa Libertadores soon.”His international career also continued, despite the fact that he had initially planned to retire after the World Cup.Instead, the 40-year-old decided he still wanted to play and was preparing in Lisbon for the start of Cape Verde's 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifying campaign.“I still feel good,” he said.There was another unexpected development waiting for him, too. With a month remaining before the Ballon d'Or ceremony, Vozinha was named among the 10 nominees for the world's best goalkeeper.“I never imagined it could happen,” he said. “It was unthinkable, but I’m grateful to those who thought of me. Just being on that list is already a great honour.”His new career has therefore brought opportunities that would have been difficult to imagine before the World Cup, from a move to Colo-Colo and the possibility of playing in the Copa Libertadores to becoming one of the most recognisable players from Cape Verde's historic campaign.But the attention has come with a price that cannot be measured in followers, contracts or endorsements.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: El Athletic explica sus cuentas
articles.standfirst: El club mantiene 94 millones de euros de liquidez y no cuenta con deuda
articles.summary: El club mantiene 94 millones de euros de liquidez y no cuenta con deuda
articles.body: El tesorero del Athletic Club, Guillermo Ruiz-Longarte, ha analizado las cuentas del club antes de la Asamblea del 28 de octubre. Cabe recordar que ayer, el Athletic anunció de manera oficial la celebración de dicha Asamblea después de que Jon Uriarte ya lo adelantase en la rueda de prensa del pasado jueves. La temporada 2025/26 se ha cerrado con un récord de 193 millones de euros de ingresos, sin ventas de jugadores, un EBITDA de 38,1 millones y un beneficio neto cercano a los 21 millones. Ruiz-Longarte ha explicado que el club ha aprovechado este resultado para realizar ajustes voluntarios y sin efecto en caja. Entre ellos figuran el adelanto de amortizaciones de jugadores y de gastos vinculados a la Fundación. El objetivo es reducir cargas futuras y dar continuidad al plan de crecimiento del Athletic durante las próximas temporadas. El escenario cambia en 2026/27. Sin competición europea, el Athletic presupuestará 152,6 millones de ingresos y una pérdida de explotación de unos 3 millones de euros. Ruiz-Longarte ha asegurado, sin embargo, que el club mantiene su apuesta por captar y retener talento para disponer de una plantilla capaz de competir al máximo nivel. Ruiz-Longarte también ha destacado la situación financiera del Athletic, que mantiene 94 millones de euros de liquidez y no cuenta con deuda. Además, el presupuesto contempla más de 15 millones de impacto positivo por traspasos y cesiones y otros 15 millones en inversiones, dentro de un proyecto que busca sostener el crecimiento económico y deportivo del club.

articles.title: El Rayo respira: Audero vuelve con Indonesia... aunque no juega
articles.standfirst: El guardameta, que no jugó el encuentro ante Singapur por unas molestias, estuvo en el banquillo frente a Malasia
articles.summary: El guardameta, que no jugó el encuentro ante Singapur por unas molestias, estuvo en el banquillo frente a Malasia
articles.body: Emil Audero volvió con Indonesia y estuvo presente desde el banquillo en el encuentro que se jugó ante Malasia el lunes 28 de septiembre. Después del contratiempo que sufrió en la previa del encuentro ante Singapur y la confirmación de sus problemas físicos por parte del seleccionador John Herdman, el guardameta volvió a entrenar con normalidad y formó parte de la nómina de jugadores convocados para el segundo partido de la Asia Cup. El resultado del encuentro fue un empate a cero en un partido en el que Indonesia se quedó con uno menos en el minuto 37 por la expulsión de Thom Haye. La cuenta oficial de la selección de Indonesia compartió unas fotos del entrenamiento previo al encuentro ante Malasia en las que se podía ver a Audero realizando los ejercicios. El seleccionador de Indonesia confirmó que valoraría el estado físico, tanto de Audero como del defensor Dean James (este jugó 82 minutos), para ver si podían disputar el encuentro. Finalmente la decisión de Herdman fue la de apostar por el jugador del Ajax, Maarten Paes, en la portería. Normalmente, él y Audero se han estado turnando en la portería de la selección asiática, por lo que la suplencia del guardameta rayista podría deberse a un motivo estrictamente táctico. El próximo encuentro de la selección de Indonesia será contra Bangladés el 1 de octubre. Buenas noticias para el Rayo Vallecano que ya perdió a Augusto Batalla en el segundo partido de liga.

articles.standfirst: El portero fue hospitalizado y estará 24 horas en observación
articles.summary: El portero fue hospitalizado y estará 24 horas en observación
articles.body: Susto importante el de esta mañana en el RCD Mallorca. Y es que el guardameta Iván 'Pichu' Cuéllar ha sido hospitalizado este lunes tras sufrir una herida de consideración en la cabeza al ser golpeado por una estructura voluminosa que se desplomó en las instalaciones de la Ciudad Deportiva Antonio Asensio. En un comunicado oficial, el club bermellón ha informado que Cuéllar “ha sufrido una herida de consideración tras el desplome de una estructura voluminosa que formaba parte de la decoración del comedor”, al parecer una gran placa desprendida de la pared, tal y como ha podido saber MARCA. En el mismo comunicado, la entidad balear ha añadido que el asturiano "permanecerá hospitalizado las próximas 24 horas en estado de observación por precaución médica". A pesar de esto, el incidente queda, aparentemente, en un susto y no se teme por el físico del jugador.

articles.body:
Última hora del Turquía - Italia en directo:

¡¡Muuuuuuuuuuuuuy buenas tardes a todos y bienvenidos a una nueva jornada de la Nations League en MARCA.com!! En algo menos de dos horas echará a rodar el balón en el Atatürk Spor Kompleksi Matl Stadyumu entre Turquía e Italia en partido correspondiente a la segunda jornada.

La selección italiana llega al choque tras perder en casa en el estreno de la 'azzurra' de Roberto Mancini en un partido donde la pegada de Bélgica dio a los de Van Bommel su primera victoria en esta fase de grupos. El nuevo proyecto no comenzó con buenas sensaciones precisamente y quedó claro que a Italia le queda un largo camino por recorrer para volver a ser una de las grandes potencias a nivel de selecciones.

Turquia , por su parte, también sucumbió en su estreno ante Francia . Bastó un solitario tanto de Mbappé en el segundo tiempo para que Zidane debutase con victoria en el mismo escenario donde hoy se miden estas dos selecciones. Los de Vincenzo Montella tratarán de hacer valer el factor casa para asestar un duro golpe a la moral italiana.

El partido promete, las dos selecciones se juegan mucho y las expectativas son importantes. Tanto para una Italia que debe empezar a ofrecer mejores sensaciones como para una Turquía que no puede dejar escapar los puntos en casa de manera consecutiva. Desde ya mismo les iremos contando todo lo que suceda... ¿Se animan a vivirlo con nosotros? ¡Venga que eeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeempezamos!
