articles.summary: FINAAAAAAAAAAL DEL PARTIDO. Gana Francia gracias al único tanto de Olise. BÉLGICA 0-1 FRANCIA Nos vamos hasta el 93. Entra Koné por Da Cunha. Se adela
articles.body:
Última hora del Bélgica - Francia en directo:

Seguimos con la UEFA Nations League y hoy tenemos uno de esos partidos que siempre prometen. Bélgica y Francia vuelven a verse las caras en la fase de grupos del torneo, tal y como hicieron en 2024, cuando los galos se impusieron en ambos encuentros. Los precedentes también sonríen a los franceses, pues no pierden ante sus vecinos desde un amistoso en 2015 y, en partido oficial, hay que remontarse hasta 1981 para encontrar la última derrota.

Bélgica llega al duelo después de superar a una pobre Italia (0-2) y sumar sus tres primeros puntos en su camino hacia los cuartos de final. Lukebakio y Godts fueron los goleadores, con este último buscando hacerse un hueco en el once de los 'Diablos Rojos' después de quedarse fuera del último Mundial. Lejos ya de aquella generación dorada, nombres como De Ketelaere, Moreira o el propio Godts están llamados a liderar el relevo, aunque todavía cuentan con el respaldo de jugadores como De Bruyne, Lukaku y Tielemans .

Francia, por su parte, también llega con una victoria tras imponerse a Turquía en el estreno de la era Zidane . El solitario tanto de Mbappé , que partió desde la izquierda, dio el triunfo a los galos, aunque con sabor agridulce. El delantero madridista se lesionó en la acción del gol y tuvo que abandonar la concentración . 'Zizou' deberá buscar ahora un sustituto para su gran estrella y cuenta con varias alternativas: Barcola, Doué y Lepaul parten como las principales opciones.

No queda nada para que ruede el balón en el Estadio Rey Balduino de Bruselas. ¡Vaaaaamooooooos!

articles.title: Campeonas del mundo con todos los honores
articles.standfirst: En Las Rozas se homenajeó a futbolistas y miembros del cuerpo técnico por la consecución del trofeo en Polonia
articles.summary: En Las Rozas se homenajeó a futbolistas y miembros del cuerpo técnico por la consecución del trofeo en Polonia
articles.body: Ayer la selección sub 20 conquistó el segundo Mundial de la categoría para España, tras superar a Corea del Norte en los penaltis. Un partido que tuvo tensión hasta el final, pero que terminó con las jugadoras de David Aznar proclamándose campeonas. Y hoy han tenido el reconocimiento merecido tras el logro. Las Rozas ha acogido a todos los miembros del equipo que han contribuido para traer el trofeo, desde las futbolistas hasta los miembros del cuerpo técnico. El acto comenzó con una 'película', contando cómo ha sido el viaje de la selección desde la fase de grupos hasta la final, con los motivadores discursos de David Aznar antes de los partidos. "Representamos a España. Nuestro nivel siempre tiene que ser alto", "Que se note lo que es España. Este Mundial no lo gana una jugadora, lo gana un equipo" o "Estoy súper orgulloso de ser entrenador de este equipo", son algunas de las palabras que dedicó el técnico a sus futbolistas antes de los encuentros. Tras ello, subieron al escenario Rafael Louzán, David Aznar, Elene Gurtubay, Noe Bejarano y Cristina Librán para hablar de la consecución del título. Fue el presidente de la Federación Española de Fútbol el primero. "Cuándo estaba sentado me estaba acordando que aquí están las campeonas del mundo y a 300 metros esta saliendo un autobús con los campeones del mundo que se van a Sevilla. Estamos probablemente ante el año de oro del fútbol español. Quedaréis para la historia de nuestro fútbol y del fútbol mundial porque es heroico lo que habéis hecho. Se valorará mucho más con el paso del tiempo. Toda España está orgullosa de esta selección. Estamos muy orgullosos de vosotras porque la misión que se nos encarga que es hacer feliz a un país se esta consiguiendo gracias a esta magnífica generación de jugadoras. Esperemos que el próximo año en Brasil podamos colocar la segunda estrella que seria coronación mundial. Enhorabuena, no tengo mas que palabras de agradecimiento", afirmó. Tras él, cogió el micro David Aznar. "Tengo la suerte de poder tener un grupo fantástico. El talento es evidente, pero son un grupo de personas increíbles que dejan su mejor versión. El compromiso ha sido al 100% desde el principio. Es una generación fantástica. Cuando llegué a la Federación no me imaginaba que me podrían hacer disfrutar tanto", dijo. Después de ellos, hablaron las jugadoras. Cristina Librán, la capitana y encargada de levantar el trofeo, fue la primera de las cuatro, señalando el buen ambiente del grupo. "Somos un poco locas, pero lo pasamos muy bien fuera del campo y se nota luego dentro. Nos gusta escuchar música, pasar tiempo juntas, pero cuanto toca entrenar estamos a tope", comentó. Irune Dorado habló sobre la 'revancha' con Corea del Norte, cuando les quitaron el Mundial sub 17 en 2024. "El fútbol te da y te quita. Sentimos un alivio al decir que hemos ganado el Mundial y decir que nos hemos quitado esa deuda que teníamos", expresó. Noe Bejarano estuvo a punto de perderse la final por la lesión que sufrió contra Brasil. Sin embargo, sabía que podía confiar en sus compañeras. "Estaba preocupada porque quería jugar, pero en el caso de no jugar sé que tengo unas compañeras que juegue quien juegue hemos demostrado que cuando salimos al campo hacemos magia, y pese a querer jugar sabia que quien saliese lo iba a hacer igual de bien", afirmó. Por último, Elene Gurtubay mandó un mensaje a las nuevas generaciones. "Tenemos una generación increíble. Somos muy amigas. Lo que le diría a las niñas más pequeñas que si quieren hacer algo que se esfuercen siempre. Transmitirles que disfruten y que se esfuercen mucho", sentenció. Tras las palabras, subieron todas las futbolistas y miembros del cuerpo técnico para recibir un obsequio conmemorativo de manos de Rafael Louzán, José Manuel Rodríguez Uribes, presidente del Consejo Superior de Deportes; Paco Díez, vicepresidente de la RFEF; y Sandra Sánchez, karateka profesional y campeona olímpica. El acto acabó con una fotografía de los personajes mencionados; todas las personas que han participado en la consecución de la Copa del Mundo; de Sonia Bermúdez, seleccionadora absoluta; y de Álvaro de Miguel, nuevo secretario general de la RFEF. Esperemos que algunas de las que han ganado el Mundial en Polonia puedan traer la segunda estrella el año que viene en Brasil.

articles.title: First time in football history: Two players sent off for pulling the same opponent with ridiculous 5ft-long dreadlocks
articles.summary: In a bizarre football match, Aedan Scipio's long dreadlocks led to two opponents being sent off for hair-pulling, marking a historic moment in football history during the Concacaf Nations League.
articles.body: Aedan Scipio had only been on the pitch for a few minutes when his extraordinary dreadlocks became the centre of a bizarre international match. The 36-year-old Anguilla forward came off the bench against Antigua and Barbuda with his side already 5–0 down, but two opponents were later sent off for pulling his hair. Both incidents involved Scipio’s ankle-length dreadlocks, turning an otherwise one-sided Concacaf Nations League match into an unusual piece of football history.Aedan Scipio’s hair became the target twiceScipio entered the match in the 69th minute at the Sir Vivian Richards Stadium, with Anguilla already facing a heavy deficit against Antigua and Barbuda.The 36-year-old, who plays for the Roaring Lions, is known for dreadlocks that stretch almost 1.5 metres and come close to his ankles when left loose. When tied back, the hair is often wrapped around his waist with a band, although even then it remains close enough to the ground to be grabbed by an opponent.That became particularly relevant in the second half.According to ESPN, Scipio had regained possession in his own area after being dispossessed when Antigua and Barbuda midfielder Keon Greene grabbed his hair and pulled him backwards. Scipio reacted angrily to the challenge, and the referee immediately showed Greene a straight red card in the 71st minute.The incident might have been strange enough on its own, but it was repeated later in the match.Deep into stoppage time, Scipio was advancing up the pitch when Antigua and Barbuda's Shalon Knight grabbed another section of his dreadlocks. The pull sent Scipio crashing to the ground, and Knight was shown a straight red card.Antigua and Barbuda finished with nine players, but the match had already produced a bizarre piece of football history: for the first time, two players had been sent off in the same game for pulling the hair of the same opponent. Both incidents involved Scipio and his extraordinary dreadlocks.Scipio became an unlikely viral sensationThe unusual sequence quickly spread online, with footage of both incidents attracting attention well beyond the Concacaf Nations League.Social-media users began referring to Anguilla as having found a "cheat code", because Scipio had entered the game with his team already five goals behind and subsequently contributed to two opposing players being dismissed.The joke, however, came from a very real physical problem created by the length of Scipio's hair.His dreadlocks are long enough to remain within an opponent's reach during a challenge, particularly when they are tied behind him. That does not make grabbing them permissible, but it helps explain why something rarely seen in professional football happened twice during the same matchScipio's appearance has also made him one of the more recognisable players in Anguilla's squad. The island nation remains among the lowest-ranked teams in international football, with ESPN reporting that Anguilla entered the match ranked 210th in the world, with only San Marino below them in FIFA's rankings.Antigua and Barbuda were ranked 163rd and entered the match as the higher-ranked side.Why hair-pulling can lead to a straight red cardThe referee's decisions were not based on Scipio having unusually long hair, but on the nature of the challenges themselves.Under football's Laws of the Game, pulling an opponent's hair can constitute violent conduct when the action involves excessive force or brutality and is not an attempt to play the ball. A sufficiently serious hair pull can therefore result in a straight red card.The issue has become more prominent in English football in recent seasons.Three Premier League players were sent off for hair-pulling incidents during the previous season, involving Wolves striker Tolu Arokodare, Everton defender Michael Keane, Sunderland's Dan Ballard and Manchester United's Lisandro Martinez in separate incidents.Keane's dismissal was subsequently appealed, with the argument made that there had not been sufficient intent or force to justify a red card. The appeal against the dismissal was unsuccessful, as was a separate attempt to have his three-match suspension reduced.The Football Association panel considering the case included three former players and voted 2–1 that the red card had not been incorrect and that a three-match suspension was not excessive.Not every contact with an opponent's hair automatically produces the same punishment. The Premier League has introduced clearer guidance under which a hair pull that is not considered excessive can result in a yellow card, while more serious conduct can be treated as violent conduct and punished with a dismissal.In Scipio's case, both Antigua and Barbuda players were sent off after physically pulling him backwards, with Knight's challenge in particular taking the Anguilla player off his feet.Antigua and Barbuda still finished with a 5–0 victoryThe two red cards did not change the outcome of the match.Antigua and Barbuda had already built a five-goal advantage before Scipio entered the game, and even after being reduced to nine players they held on to win 5–0 at the Sir Vivian Richards Stadium.The victory came in League C, Group B of the Concacaf Nations League, giving Jacques Passy's side a comfortable result despite the extraordinary finish.For Anguilla, the scoreline remained the dominant fact of the night, but Scipio's brief cameo ensured that the match would be remembered for something else as well.Antigua and Barbuda will now face the consequences of losing Greene and Knight to suspension, with both players set to miss the next meeting with Anguilla on Friday.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: La propuesta de sanción al City: sin descenso... pero con 'trabas' para entrar en Champions
articles.standfirst: The Athletic revela que un antiguo directivo de la Premier propuso una sanción de puntos diferida en varias temporadas
articles.summary: The Athletic revela que un antiguo directivo de la Premier propuso una sanción de puntos diferida en varias temporadas
articles.body: La sanción al Manchester City caerá de un momento a otro... por más que vaya a haber apelación al respecto. El proceso todavía va para largo. Sin embargo, ya se está empezando a moldear ciertas propuestas de sanción que varían entre una enorme escala de grises. The Athletic fue quien destapó la culpabilidad del conjunto 'skyblue' el pasado viernes y, días más tarde, han conversado con un exdirectivo de la Premier League que ha desvelado cuál fue la propuesta de sanción que presentó en el momento que se destapó todo este escándalo, allá por 2023. "Hablé con un antiguo directivo de alto rango de la Premier League. Su idea consistía, básicamente, en que durante las próximas tres a cinco temporadas se les restaran entre 20 y 25 puntos por temporada, lo que, en la práctica, haría casi imposible que se clasificaran para la Champions durante ese periodo, dejándolos, en el mejor de los casos, en una especie de 'isla' en la zona media de la tabla durante los próximos tres a cinco años", expuso Adam Crafton en dicho 'podcast' de The Athletic. De momento, todo son especulaciones alrededor del conocido como 'juicio del siglo'. Todavía queda mucha tela por cortar hasta conocer cuál será la sanción definitiva que se le acabe imponiendo al Manchester City.

articles.title: Spain vs Croatia: UEFA Nations League – Yamal, Modric, teams, form
articles.summary: World champions Spain host Croatia in matchday two of the UEFA Nations League, with Yamal facing Modric.
articles.body:
Who : Spain vs Croatia What : UEFA Nations League 2026-27 , Group A3 match Where : Ramon Sanchez-Pizjuan Stadium, Seville, Spain When : Tuesday, September 28, at 8:45pm (18:45 GMT) How to follow : Al Jazeera Sport will bring you all the build-up and live updates from 15:45 GMT.

A battle of generations awaits on Tuesday, as 19-year-old superstar Lamine Yamal faces 41-year-old midfield maestro Luka Modric in Spain’s Nations League clash with Croatia.

The meeting in Seville comes after both sides made a winning start to their respective campaigns – Spain staged a 3-2 comeback win over England in London, while Croatia defeated Czechia 2-1 in Prague.

World champions Spain, who are on a 39-game winning streak – a record for a European team – are bidding for their second Nations League title after their 2023 success.

As the finalists last year, La Roja face a tricky task in matchday two against a well-balanced Croatian side, led by the evergreen Modric, who was the architect of their opening victory.

The UEFA Nations League was founded in 2018 to reduce the number of meaningless friendlies and give nations competitive matches against top-ranked teams.

In this competition, countries from across Europe participate in a league structure, which features promotion and relegation.

They last played against each other at the UEFA Euro 2024 in a group game, with Spain beating Croatia 3-0 , thanks to goals from Alvaro Morata, Fabian Ruiz and Dani Carvajal.

Lamine Yamal and Dani Olmo (Spain): Yamal, already a world-famous footballer at 19, needed only two minutes to find the net against England before wrapping up a man-of-the-match quality performance. The Barcelona winger is enjoying a strong start this season, with his seven goals rated joint-second-highest in La Liga. His club teammate, Olmo, also played a role in Spain’s latest victory with a useful assist; watch out for him.

Luka Modric and Ivan Perisic (Croatia): Even at 41, Modric is showing no signs of slowing down after the captain scored the opener in Croatia’s first win in coach Slaven Bilic’s first game back in charge. Two decades on from his international debut, Modric still pulls the strings in midfield and cannot be overlooked. Apart from him, fans should watch out for another experienced player, Ivan Perisic, who set up the winner in the last game and has two goals and an assist for PSV Eindhoven this season.

Luis de la Fuente (Spain coach) : “What this generation of footballers is achieving has great merit. They are constantly striving to improve. The statistics speak for themselves. It is incredibly difficult what Spain are doing. We will approach the next match against Croatia as if it was our last. These players always want to keep improving.”

Slaven Bilic (Croatia coach): “Luka Modric … We can only be proud that we live in his era and have the privilege to watch him play. At his age, he is incredible and the only one who can do what he’s doing, you know what I mean.”

Goalkeeper Joan Garcia is sidelined until early October due to a knee injury, while defender Eric Garcia, who withdrew from the squad after feeling discomfort in his knee in the last game’s warm-up, has been replaced by Robin Le Normand.

Probable Spain XI: Unai Simon; Marc Pubill, Pau Cubarsi, Aymeric Laporte, Marc Cucurella; Rodri, Fabian Ruiz; Lamine Yamal, Dani Olmo, Nico Williams; Ferran Torres

Left winger Martin Baturina and right-back Josip Juranovic are out with illness, while centre-back Martin Erlic is injured.

Probable Croatia XI : Dominik Livakovic; Josip Stanisic, Luka Vuskovic, Josko Gvardiol, Ivan Perisic; Luka Modric, Mateo Kovacic; Luka Sucic, Petar Sucic, Franjo Ivanovic; Igor Matanovic

articles.title: De la Fuente: "Claro que me gustaría ganar el Balón de Oro, que tomen nota"
articles.standfirst: Rueda de prensa del seleccionador español en la previa del partido ante Croacia
articles.summary: Rueda de prensa del seleccionador español en la previa del partido ante Croacia
articles.body: Luis de la Fuente ha comparecido en la sala de prensa del Ramón Sánchez-Pizjuán para analizar el partido ante Croacia. Y lo que es su regreso al que fue su estadio como jugador y como entrenador. El partido de Wembley: "Este equipo tienen muchos registros, pero siempre con una idea reconocible. Tenemos muchas opciones de jugar de diferente manera. Siempre tratamos de sacar el mejor rendimiento de los jugadores". Rotaciones: "Si te digo que no, hay debate (entre risas). Es razonable que habrá algunos cambios. Por refrescar el equipo y porque cualquiera de los 26 puede jugar. Mañana entendemos que habrá que dar energía en algunas demarcaciones. Los jugadores están todos en perfectas condiciones". Balón de Oro de los entrenadores: "No sé el criterio para votar. Quiero que gane un español. En el apartado de futbolistas y de técnicos. Todos hemos hecho méritos. Somos cuatro. Yo estoy feliz de estar nominado". Fermín: "Está en un estado de forma fantástico, como otros compañeros. Es polivalente. Nos da energía, vitalidad, intensidad, talento, clase... Ese tipo de jugador es necesario". Formato: "Cualquiera entiende que jugar cuatro partidos en 10 días es muy exigente. Nosotros hemos demostrado que siempre pensamos en la salud de los futbolistas. Hemos preferido que Eric recupere ¿Qué diría al entrenador que llegó al Sevilla?: "Evolución como entrenador. "Hay veces que digo que no me reconozco cuando empecé e a entrenar. Hemos ido cambiando muchos aspectos. Yo le diría a aquel Luis de hace 25 años que no baje los brazos y que siga siendo constante. La vida me ha desmotrado que haciendo eso tienes oportunidades". ¿Cómo están los jugadores?: "Los 26 están todos al 100%". Más del Balón de Oro: "Estoy orgulloso y feliz de estar ahí. Tenemos los mismos méritos que el resto para ganarlo. Me haría mucha ilusión, me encantaría. Que tomen nota: me encantaría ganarlo". Croacia: "Claro que tienen posibilidades. No hay rival ni día perfecto. Jugamos contra una selección croata que conocemos muy bien y con jugadores con mucho talento. Va a ser un partido donde habrá que dar una mejor versión que en Londres contra Inglaterra". El grupo: "Desde que soy seleccionador, los jugadores que más partidos deciden son los que salen desde el banquillo. El otro día lo dijo Merino, queremos sensación de equipo. Todos tienen derecho a jugar porque son muy buenos. Son los mejores jugadores del mundo". Eric García: "Si estuviéramos en una fase final se hubiera quedado. Todos hubiéramos asumido ese riesgo. Para mañana no hubiera estado y, de cara al tercer partido, podía estar, o no. No merecía la pena correr ese riesgo. En ningún caso íbamos a buscar un conflicto con el futbolista". Locura con la selección: "Es un orgullo. Hemos recuperado el espíritu de 2010. La gente está orgullosa de sentirse española. Estoy honrado de ser el seleccionador de mi país. Estar en Sevilla me produce una emoción muy especial. Sevilla es una ciudad muy especial en mi vida".

articles.title: Fabián Ruiz: "Aquí miramos más a lo colectivo que a lo individual"
articles.standfirst: Rueda de prensa del centrocampista de la selección y del PSG
articles.summary: Rueda de prensa del centrocampista de la selección y del PSG
articles.body: Fabián Ruiz, el jugador que nunca ha perdido con España (51 partidos) ha sido el elegido por la selección para hablar el nombre del vestuario antes del partido ante Croacia. En su tierra, aunque en terrtorio rival para un bético, ha tomado la palabra. Racha sin perder: "Muy contento por esa estadística. Eso quiere decir que llevamos mucho tiempo sin perder. Ojalá podamos seguir así mucho tiempo. No me gusta compararme con la selección de 2010. Ojala ganar Eurocopa, Mundial y Eurocopa como ellos". La suya y Marchena: "No sabía hasta hace un rato que estoy cerca de Marchena (tiene 57). Ojalá superarlo por un buen motivo". Balón de Oro: "No se trata de hacer campaña, se trata de reconocer tu trabajo. He tenido un gran año ganando las competiciones más importantes. Cuando lo hacéis bien y vendéis muchos periódicos queréis que se reconozca. Nosotros también". Mejor equipo: "Además de ser un gran equipo tenemos grandes jugadores. Las dos cosas te llevan al éxito. Miramos más por lo colectivo que por lo individual". Betis: "Sigo al Betis siempre que puedo. Me alegro de todo lo bien que le vaya. Soy bético, todo el mundo lo sabe. Me gustaría terminar mi carrera aquí. Seguro que en el futuro se puede". Recuerdo del Pizjuán: "Fue un día mágico, el primer derbi que gané. Marqué y ganamos. Era el día de Reyes y fue muy bonito". Palabras de Kovacic: "Todo el mundo sabe lo bueno que es. Lo ha demostrado en todos los equipos que ha ido. Tiene una grandísima calidad. Es un jugador a tener en cuenta porque sabemos el peligro que nos puede crear. Es muy difícil quitarle la pelota". Pedri. "La relación es magnífica. Sabemos que lo importante es el colectivo. Estamos aquí para ayudar. Estoy agradecido por la confianza. Para jugar tengo que estar al 100%."

articles.title: El Valladolid intenta evitar otro 'caso Chuki' con Arnu
articles.standfirst: Oferta de renovación al canterano, que se estrenó como goleador ante el Córdoba
articles.summary: Oferta de renovación al canterano, que se estrenó como goleador ante el Córdoba
articles.body: Los más jóvenes de la plantilla del Real Valladolid resultaron clave en la victoria ante el Córdoba en la última jornada. A los estrenos goleadores del vallisoletano Víctor Fernández Jr, cedido por el Valencia, y del canterano culé Víctor Barberá, fichado en propiedad, se unió el buen hacer de Adrián Arnu. El delantero no sólo realizó un gran partido y tiró del equipo blanquivioleta para obrar la remontada, sino que fue el autor del tanto del empate en la primera parte y, además, asistió a Víctor Jr en el 2-1 tras una gran jugada en la segunda. Consciente del crecimiento de sus canteranos en el primer equipo, el club pucelano ya se ha puesto manos a la obra para retener a algunos como el propio Arnu. Tal y como ha podido saber MARCA, el futbolista tiene encima de la mesa desde hace aproximadamente un mes una oferta para renovar su contrato, el cual finaliza el próximo 30 de junio. Ante el temor de que pueda darse otro 'caso Chuki', quien se marchó libre al Werder Bremen en el último mercado de fichajes, el Real Valladolid se ha apresurado a plantear la renovación al palentino antes de que pueda firmar por cualquier otro club a partir del 1 de enero. La intención del Pucela es ampliar el contrato de Arnu al menos dos temporadas más y, de inicio, el delantero ha mostrado su predisposición total a poder firmar más pronto que tarde la prolongación de su vinculación. Tras pasar a formar parte del primer equipo vallisoletano hace dos años, y ante la falta de minutos, el punta fue cedido al Real Madrid C en el pasado mercado invernal. Sin embargo, allí tampoco disfrutó de demasiadas oportunidades y el club blanco no ejerció la opción de compra reflejada en el acuerdo. De vuelta a casa, tras convertirse en titular en el duelo en Ceuta, repetir ante el Córdoba en el José Zorrilla y estrenar su cuenta goleadora, Arnu parece haber encontrado su sitio en un Real Valladolid que ha decidido plantearle una oferta de renovación.

articles.title: Man City charges: CEO Ferran Soriano issues defiant message to European club bosses
articles.summary: Manchester City chief executive Ferran Soriano issues a defiant message to the executives of other teams about the club being found guilty of a majority of Premier League charges, BBC Sport has been told.
articles.body:
Manchester City chief executive Ferran Soriano has issued a defiant message to the executives of other teams about the club being found guilty of a majority of Premier League charges, BBC Sport has been told.

He was speaking at a board meeting of European Football Clubs (formerly the ECA) in Copenhagen before its general assembly on Tuesday.

Soriano was said to have vowed to fight the charges and the process had a long way to run, reiterating what the club's chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak said in a letter to fans .

The Press Association reported Soriano told the executives "it's taken eight years to get here and it's going to take a lot more time", referring to the start of the Premier League's investigation in 2018.

He then left the meeting without answering any questions from the media.

The report added Manchester United 's chief of international football relations Jean-Claude Blanc and Everton owner Dan Friedkin - there in his capacity as owner of Roma - were among those to attend.

City were accused of a wide range of rule breaches, centering around claims they inflated sponsorship revenue from connected companies and made other "off the books" payments to circumvent financial regulations.

On Friday, it emerged they had been found guilty of the vast majority of the 115 charges brought against them.

Premier League clubs are seeking legal advice about compensation relating to the charges, while BBC Sport has been told City will appeal.

Sanctions are yet to be announced, but repercussions could include a points deduction, expulsion from the top flight or a huge fine.

The Premier League has declined to comment, while City released a statement saying the "Premier League process remains ongoing with significant elements to be completed, and subject to strict confidentiality".

Chairman Al Mubarak told supporters on Saturday he was confident the club would prove their innocence.

"The Premier League process still has a long way to run, and our confidence and intent in proving the club's innocence is just as strong as when this began," he said.

"There are so many things that I would like to be able to share with you to help you understand why we feel so confident in our position.

"But the strict confidentiality of the legal process and our determination to respect it means I cannot do that at the moment. Even this letter underwent several legal checks to make sure it complies."

articles.title: Man City ruling: Joe Harts trusts club chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak's claims they are innocent of breaking Premier League's financial rules
articles.summary: Former Manchester City goalkeeper Joe Hart believes club chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak's claims they are innocent of breaking the Premier League's financial rules.
articles.body:
Former Manchester City goalkeeper Joe Hart believes club chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak's claims they are innocent of breaking financial rules.

City have been found guilty of the majority of 115 breaches of financial rules they had been accused of by the Premier League, although they are set to appeal against the ruling.

Al Mubarak said he is still committed to "proving the club's innocence" and the "process still has a long way to run".

Hart, who made 348 appearances for City in all competitions between 2006 and 2016, told BBC Radio 5 Live's Monday Night Club Al Mubarak was someone who has "led the club brilliantly" and is a person to "trust".

"I've heard everyone else go down every single rabbit hole, every single wormhole, every single discussion," Hart said.

"My honest opinion is I've got no reason not to trust Khaldoon. What he said is enough for me.

"I loved how he spoke. I loved the letter because that was from someone who cared about the club."

Man City CEO defiant over Premier League charges

The computer hacker who tried to take down Man City

The four 'what next?' scenarios for Premier League after Man City ruling

Hart twice won the Premier League (2011-12 and 2013-14) and League Cup (2013-14 and 2015-16) as well as the FA Cup (2010-11) during his time at City.

The 39-year-old said because there was "nothing concrete", it was matter of allowing things to "play out" and none of his achievements are in any way tarnished.

Hart added: "If Man City are found guilty, which I don't think they are because of what Khaldoon said, then there's conversations to be had.

"But right now I'm very confident and very, very calm. I'm very proud of what I've achieved and what I did with Manchester City and what we achieved as a team. And that doesn't change. That doesn't change until you tell me."

City were accused of a wide range of rule breaches, centering around claims they inflated sponsorship revenue from connected companies and made other "off the books" payments to circumvent financial regulations.

Hart said it hadn't "crossed my mind" to talk about the news with his former City team-mates because he "can't get involved in the ifs, buts and maybes".

"I did what I did. I lined up 11 v 11 and had it out on the pitch. I won some games, lost some games, drew some games, and I shook hands and I walked off," he said.

"I know what I did, I know what we did, and I know how it happened. It didn't feel like we were scheming or plotting."

articles.title: England: Thomas Tuchel claims Three Lions were a danger to themselves in possession as he plays down defensive frailties
articles.summary: England boss Thomas Tuchel has played down concerns over his side defensively after their 3-2 defeat to Spain; England have conceded nine goals in their last three games; follow Czech Republic vs England with the Sky Sports website and App on Tuesday, kick-off 7.45pm
articles.body:
The Three Lions made several crucial mistakes in their loss to the reigning world and European champions on Saturday and were made to pay with goals from Lamine Yamal, Alex Baena and Mikel Oyarzabal.

Having gone the whole of the World Cup qualifying campaign without conceding, Tuchel's side have now let in nine from their last three internationals against Argentina, France and Spain.

Despite showing frailties against elite opposition, Tuchel does not think England's issue lies with their defensive set-up and instead insists that their mistakes have come from causing their own issues in possession.

"It's not a concern yet," Tuchel said ahead of England's second Nations League game against Czech Republic on Tuesday.

"I felt that in terms of organised defending, block defending and active defending, we were at a higher level than in many other matches.

"If you want to look at it in isolation on how we did within the structure and in the units of the sides, I was quite happy and I think it was a step ahead.

"We suffered clearly from individual mistakes when we had the ball, especially in the deep build-up, so that is of course something we cannot repeat. Not at this level.

"Strangely enough, when we had the ball, we were the biggest danger to ourselves around the box because we just had too many individual mistakes. Purely in defending, I have no concerns and I trust that we can do it."

Tuchel's comments come off the back of widespread criticism of his tactics during England's World Cup semi-final defeat to Argentina, where he opted to defend a one-goal lead rather than looking to extend their advantage.

The German responded by hitting out at the 'DNA' of English players. "I think ball possession plays a crucial role; it's maybe not in our DNA like it is in Spanish DNA or in Argentinian-Brazilian DNA, to take the ball and control the game with the ball," he said following their exit.

It raised scrutiny over England's footballing identity, but Tuchel believed his players showcased exactly that in the defeat to Luis de la Fuente's side at Wembley.

"I think there was a lot of discussion about this before [the Spain game]," Tuchel stated.

"I think we showed our style and we showed our courage. The players showed an identity and they showed it throughout the 90 minutes.

"We gave them a lot of problems. We caused ourselves some problems with individual mistakes. Mistakes can sometimes happen. They shouldn't, but they did happen.

"We had the world and European champions on the edge of a defeat. In the decisive moments we played our best football. We kept attacking when we were a goal ahead. We were even more dominant and more of a threat.

"We were a little bit self-responsible for the break in momentum towards the end of the match. But overall we have a lot of positives to take away."

articles.body: La Selección Española de fútbol continúa su camino en la UEFA Nations League con su esperado segundo compromiso de la fase de grupos. Tras el debut frente a Inglaterra en Londres con victoria por 2-3, el combinado nacional regresa a territorio nacional para enfrentarse a la combativa selección de Croacia en un duelo crucial por el liderato del Grupo A3 de la Liga A. El encuentro se disputará el próximo martes 29 de septiembre a las 20:45 horas. Este horario unificado fijado por la UEFA para los compromisos de la competición garantiza una velada de máxima expectación futbolística. El escenario elegido para albergar esta cita de nivel internacional es el Estadio Ramón Sánchez-Pizjuán, ubicado en la ciudad de Sevilla. La capital andaluza volverá a convertirse en el feudo de La Roja, que se ha acostumbrado a ver partido allí en La Cartuja. El España - Croacia de la segunda jornada de la Nations League se disputará a las 20:45 horas. Todos los aficionados podrán seguir el desarrollo del choque en directo y en abierto a través de La 1 de Televisión Española, así como en streaming a través de la plataforma digital RTVE Play.

articles.title: Will key LSU players sit for McNeese game? Here's what Lane Kiffin said
articles.summary: In the wake of injuries piling up for his team, does LSU football coach Lane Kiffin consider sitting key players for McNeese game?
articles.body:
BATON ROUGE — What has transpired for LSU football over the past two weeks has had Lane Kiffin feeling down.

Three key players have gone down with significant injuries. Despite losing stars Trey'Dez Green , Whit Weeks and Dashawn Spears , No. 11 LSU (3-1) was able to go 1-1 while the injury bug took a big bite of the team, with LSU most recently taking down Texas A&M 35-6 at home Saturday night.

LSU quarterback Sam Leavitt also tweaked his left hamstring in the win over the Aggies .

Because of the injuries and how the schedule sets up after facing McNeese State on Saturday, Oct. 3 for Kiffin's team going forward with seven SEC games remaining, four of those being road contests, it has caused the head coach to have to think differently.

One of those thoughts is possibly sitting some of LSU's key players against McNeese (6:45 p.m. CT, SEC Network) on Saturday inside Tiger Stadium.

LSU football romps Texas A&M to get back on track

"Yeah, I've been going through that all day yesterday," Kiffin said Monday when The Daily Advertiser asked if he considered sitting some of the team's key players this weekend. "I don't know where we're going to end up on that but, like I said, we got seven conference games to go, four more road conference games. Five of those seven probably (against) ranked (teams).

"You got to look at things differently, I feel like, because of what's happened."

There's been plenty of shifting around for the Tigers the past two weeks in the wake of players getting hurt. And now, coaches are looking at guys that might not have filled the roles they're occupying now and playing different or multiple positions for the team.

"Everyone knows the one for one, which person starts in place of these guys. But it's much more than that. It's now some of those guys were playing multiple (spots), starting on special teams. Now they come off of that," Kiffin said. "Now the backup special teams guys got to step up to play that.

"It's a lot of people needing to do their job when significant injuries happen. They just affect a lot of different parts and even sometimes they affect how you call the game and what you have to do."

Kiffin hasn't decided on holding Leavitt or some of LSU's other key players out against McNeese just yet. But he has said multiple times that he hasn't coached a team that's had this many significant injuries this early in the season.

And during the A&M game Saturday night, it began to spook him.

"Extremely (cautious). I think I mean I'm human. With what's happened with these freak injuries, it's tough," Kiffin said. "I took our guys out earlier in the (Texas A&M) game than I did in the previous home game because of what was going on and that just freaked me out. We'll be extremely cautious this week all around because it's the schedule you play with. Once you go to nine (conference games), it's another SEC game.

"It feels like we've played a whole season already and we have seven SEC games to go."

Cory Diaz covers the LSU Tigers for The Daily Advertiser as part of the USA TODAY Network. Follow his Tigers coverage on Twitter: @ByCoryDiaz. Got questions regarding LSU athletics? Send them to Cory Diaz at bdiaz@gannett.com .

articles.title: Lamine Yamal blesses Barcelona youngster: ‘He’ll score a lot of goals’
articles.summary: Barcelona star Lamine Yamal has this week tipped a fellow member of the club’s attacking ranks to go on to enjoy a productive stint in Catalunya’s capital.Th...
articles.body:
Barcelona star Lamine Yamal has this week tipped a fellow member of the club's attacking ranks to go on to enjoy a productive stint in Catalunya's capital.

The player in question? Hamza Abdelkarim.

Frontman Abdelkarim for his part spent this past summer sparking widespread excitement amongst those of a Barcelona persuasion. After his loan arrival from Al Ahly was made permanent, the Egyptian was afforded the chance to impress at senior level by Hansi Flick in pre-season.

And this is an opportunity which Abdelkarim went on to grasp with both hands, finding the net several times in limited playing time across the Blaugrana 's friendly fixture list.

Such exploits have since culminated in a La Liga debut, as excitement surrounding the talents of a player still just 18 years of age continues to mount.

Speaking during an interview with On Sport (as cited by Diario Sport ) early this week, the aforementioned Lamine Yamal was therefore drawn on the name of his breakthrough teammate. And the World Cup winner was full of praise in his response:

"He is a player with a bright future ahead of him. He's still young and has all the qualities to be a great striker. I think he will make the most of his time in the team and score a lot of goals.

"We have all seen it; He is a striker who scores a lot of goals. He will benefit from the time he plays at Barcelona. He is a very adaptable player. We make a great team. We always try to make him feel comfortable."

articles.title: Lo del Castellón no se veía hace 14 años... y acabó en ascenso
articles.standfirst: El Elche, en la temporada 2012-2013, fue el último equipo de Segunda que sumó 19 puntos en las siete primeras jornadas
articles.summary: El Elche, en la temporada 2012-2013, fue el último equipo de Segunda que sumó 19 puntos en las siete primeras jornadas
articles.body: El Castellón está a un nivel altísimo. Ganó en Leganés (0-2) con autoridad y ya son cuatro jornadas seguidas liderando LaLiga Hypermotion. El equipo orellut no conoce la derrota y sólo ha cedido un empate (0-0 contra el Sabadell en Castalia). De esta manera, ha sumado 19 puntos de 21 posibles, una cifra brutal en una categoría tan igualada como la Segunda española. Para encontrar un registro tan espectacular hay que retroceder hasta la temporada 2012-2013. También lo firmó un equipo de la Comunidad Valenciana, el Elche, entrenado por entonces por Fran Escribá. ¿Y cómo terminó aquello? Con los franjiverdes siendo campeones y ascendiendo a Primera 24 años después. ¿Se repetirá la historia? Los de Castalia, que la campaña pasada disputaron los playoffs, no pisan la élite desde 1991. El equipo de Pablo Hernández también es el mejor equipo visitante de la Hypermotion. Lo ha ganado todo fuera: 0-1 a la Real Sociedad B, 1-2 al Celta Fortuna, 1-2 al Girona y 0-2 al Leganés. El Eibar también ha hecho pleno lejos de Ipurua, pero ha disputado un encuentro menos que los blanquinegros.

articles.title: Un Castellón muy superior aprovecha los errores del Lega y se consolida líder
articles.standfirst: Morata desperdició una clamorosa ocasión, Luca Zidane falló fuera del área y Suero marcó un golazo, mientras Jakobsen cerró el triunfo y Millán falló un penalti
articles.summary: Morata desperdició una clamorosa ocasión, Luca Zidane falló fuera del área y Suero marcó un golazo, mientras Jakobsen cerró el triunfo y Millán falló un penalti
articles.body: Avance. Un Castellón bastante superior se impuso en Butarque aprovechando además los fallos de un Leganés que cede así los primeros puntos ante su afición. Mientras Morata desperdició dos ocasiones muy claras, Luca Zidane falló en el primer gol y Álex Millán desperdició un penalti, los visitantes marcaron las diferencias con el golazo de Suero y otro de Jakobsen para su cuarta victoria consecutiva y su cuarto triunfo en otros tantos desplazamientos que le permiten consolidarse al frente de la clasificación. Al descanso se llegó con ventaja 'orellut' tras una primera parte marcada por dos errores, el de Morata, que desperdició una ocasión clamorosa nada más empezar el partido tras pase de Soko, y el de Luca Zidane, que 'regaló' el balón fuera del área a Suero y éste lo aprovechó con una soberbia parábola desde casi 30 metros. Y eso que el meta pepinero le había hecho dos grandes paradas antes a Jakobsen y Ousmane Camara, ante el que repitió otra de mucho mérito justo antes del descanso. Zico tuvo el empate para el Lega, con una volea tras un córner que salió cerca del poste, y Soko con un cabezazo que despejó Matthys, mientras el Castellón pudo ampliar diferencias por medio de Barri y del propio Camara y de Jakobsen, ambos por partida doble. Pero nada más comenzar el segundo tiempo el equipo 'orellut' no falló más y Jakobsen puso el 2-0 con un disparo cruzado después de una gran carrera tras un taconazo de Suero en el centro del campo. Soko estuvo cerca de meter al Lega en el partido, pero su vaselina salió rozando el larguero, mientras Morata, a puerta vacía, no supo aprovechar a bote pronto el error de Matthys en el despeje. Lo siguió intentando hasta el final el Lega, Naim y Suleiman no acertaron, pero se pudo meter en el partido tras una patada de Mellot en la cara a Unax del Cura que significó la roja para el lateral visitante y penalti, pero Álex Millán no lo convirtió, ya que Matthys le hizo una gran parada.

articles.title: Can Wisconsin handle success? Fickell pushes team to continue grind after upset win
articles.summary: The Badgers beat a ranked team on the road last week. Now they have to reset and prepare for a Homecoming matchup with Michigan State.
articles.body:
MADISON – In the span of one week, Wisconsin 's situation has flipped.

The Badgers football team, fresh off a comeback win at Penn State , is a 10½-point favorite to beat Michigan State when they play Oct. 3 at Camp Randall Stadium (11:30 a.m. kickoff; Big Ten Network). Last week UW was a 10-point underdog against the Nittany Lions .

While point spreads aren't a true gauge of a team's talent, they are a sign of public sentiment, and the Badgers ' stock is on the rise after a big victory.

The key for the team will be to go about its business as if its a bear market.

"We're a team that has still continued to climb," Badgers coach Luke Fickell said Sept. 28 during his weekly press conference at Camp Randall Stadium. "Nothing has changed in the way we go about our business and so that's where for the first time, we've got to be able to handle some success and some positives and keep us going in the right direction."

The 24-20 win over Penn State gave the Badgers their first victory in Happy Valley since 2003 and snapped a six-game losing streak dating back to 2012 against the Nittany Lions overall.

The victory was also UW's highest-ranked win on the road since a 38-17 triumph at No. 9 Minnesota on Nov. 30, 2019.

That said, the film review probably brought the Badgers down to Earth, particularly the offense. In addition to Colton Joseph 's three interceptions, the Badgers committed five false-start penalties and were flagged a season-high nine times overall. Their third-down conversion rate of 26.7% (4 for 15) was also a season low.

"We know we've got to be able to play better," Fickell said. "And a lot of people will ask questions and point at the quarterback play. We know we have to play better, got to make better decisions at the quarterback position.

"But I think that there's a lot of other things that go into that. We've got to do a better job as a whole on helping our quarterback out. And so it's not just falling on the shoulders of the quarterback."

Wisconsin football schedule 2026, see Badgers' opponents, game dates

Fickell's respect for Michigan State Pat Fitzgerald runs deep

The Spartans come to town after suffering a 31-13 loss to Nebraska on Sept. 26 that also cost the team its top running back. First-year coach Pat Fitzgerald announced Sept. 28 that running back Cam Edwards will miss the remainder of the season due to what appeared to be a knee injury.

Edwards was one of the 62 newcomers Fitzgerald added to the program after he was hired in December.

Fitzgerald and Fickell played college ball at essentially the same time and have coached in the Big Ten for years as either a head coach or assistant.

That said, Fickell has respected Fitzgerald from afar due to his work at Northwestern and as president of the American Football Coaches Association.

"It's unique to see him not in the colors that he had worn for so many years," Fickell said. "But I know that he's building something, and I have the utmost respect for him."

Fickell praises impact of fans at Camp Randall Stadium

The matchup will be Wisconsin 's conference home opener and a chance to see what impact the Penn State victory has on fan attendance.

The announced attendance of 65,274 for the season opener was the lowest for the program since 1992. The attendance for Game 2 against Eastern Illinois was only slightly better (66,545).

This week UW will have a chance to ride the wave of that victory plus Homecoming weekend and what is expected to be good weather.

Fickell cited the environment of UW's last two home games – wins over Washington and Illinois last season – as examples of the positive impact the fans at Camp Randall can have on his team.

"Sometimes you think it's just if you can create a raucous environment like we were in last week, it makes it really difficult on the opposing team," Fickell said. "Well, you don't understand how much energy it gives to your team as well and so I think there's a balance there that we want to continue to create.

"We know we have a part in having success and playing better and putting the product out there that makes everybody excited to create those environments … Hopefully we can build upon the things that we've done and we'll have one of those this weekend."

articles.title: Arsenal star says injury could have ended his career
articles.summary: Mikel Merino recovered from a serious injury to star for Spain at the 2026 World Cup, having suggested that the setback could have ended his career.The midfi...
articles.body:
Mikel Merino recovered from a serious injury to star for Spain at the 2026 World Cup, having suggested that the setback could have ended his career.

The midfielder is an important player for both club and country, but there was a chance he would miss the World Cup. He returned only a few weeks before the squad was named and did not play much for Arsenal during the final weeks of the campaign.

Some fans were surprised that Merino made the Spain squad, but their manager remained committed to a player with whom he had enjoyed significant success. Merino's inclusion ultimately proved important for Spain during the competition.

Merino will now be looking to play an important role for Arsenal in the league this season, while also putting his injury problems from the previous campaign behind him.

Arsenal will not want to lose him to another injury because he is such a valuable player. His ability to operate in both attack and midfield gives the Gunners additional options in different areas of the pitch.

The midfielder's recovery was particularly significant because of the uncertainty surrounding his return. Having been sidelined for a considerable period, he had to work his way back into contention before the World Cup.

His experience also appears to have changed his perspective beyond football. The uncertainty he faced during his recovery made him consider the possibility that he might not be able to return to the sport, giving him a different outlook on his career.

Speaking about his ordeal, Merino reflected on the mental challenge of dealing with uncertainty and the possibility that his football career could be interrupted permanently.

"There's going to be a moment when you'll have to fight against the uncertainty of not knowing if you'll ever play football again.

"It taught me how to deal with frustration. That opened my eyes, made me accept that I'm not just a footballer and that there's much more to life."

Merino can now focus on continuing his career with Arsenal after overcoming the setback. His versatility remains an important asset, and the club will hope he can maintain his fitness throughout the season.

articles.title: Broadcast information announced for Red River Showdown
articles.summary: OU-Texas has received its TV channel designation.
articles.body:
The Oklahoma Sooners and the Texas Longhorns will renew perhaps the greatest rivalry in all of sports on Saturday, October 10th, and while the kickoff time for the Red River Rivalry has been known for months now, we now know what TV channel the game will air on.

According to the SEC's press release on Monday, ABC will broadcast the game, which will kick off at 2:30 p.m. CT. The announcing team for the game at the neutral site in Dallas is not yet known. Texas is the designated visiting team for this year's matchup, with Oklahoma as the designated home team, as they are for each even year in the Cotton Bowl. This game will be Oklahoma's first appearance on ABC this season.

Both teams will be coming off of their bye weeks as they enter this matchup, and while top-ranked Texas is 4-0 and surging to start the year, unranked Oklahoma is 2-2 and struggling to open the season. Last year, unranked Texas already had two losses and sat at 3-2 coming into South Dallas, but they still won by 17 over the 5-0 and sixth-ranked Sooners.

It was Texas' second-straight win in the rivalry series, but Oklahoma made the College Football Playoff last season, while the Longhorns were left out. Now, OU looks to return the favor on ABC at the State Fair of Texas in 2026.

articles.title: Vozinha yearning for 'the life I had before' as World Cup hero struggles with newfound fame
articles.summary: Men's Goalkeeper of the Year nominee and Cape Verde international Vozinha has admitted to struggling with his newfound fame following his heroics at this sum...
articles.body:
Every edition of the FIFA World Cup sees players emerge with newfound fame thanks to individual moments of brilliance, and nobody epitomises this more so than Cape Verde goalkeeper Vozinha .

The 40-year-old has enjoyed a journeyman career playing in Angola, Moldova, Portugal , Cyprus, Slovakia, and of course, in the West African archipelago nation of Cape Verde.

A free agent entering what was Cape Verde's first-ever World Cup this summer in North America, after his time with Portuguese second-division side Chaves came to a close, Vozinha faced an uncertain future. However, his World Cup debut proved not only a performance to remember for both him and his teammates, but also a life-changing event for the now 93-time international.

Cape Verde were tasked with opening their campaign against reigning UEFA European champions and eventual tournament winners, Spain , and to say they defied all expectations would be an understatement. A 0-0 draw, thanks in no small part to some excellent saves from Vozinha, helped Cape Verde become one of the darlings of the tournament.

Vozinha's raw emotion once the final whistle blew quickly went viral, along with clips of his heroics in goal. Within the blink of an eye, his following on Instagram began to skyrocket, going from 56,000 pre-game to 28.3 million as of September 28.

Draws against Uruguay and Saudi Arabia sent Cape Verde into the Round of 32, where their remarkable run came to an equally memorable ending, losing 3-2 in extra time to reigning champions and eventual finalists Argentina - despite one of the goals of the tournament from Sidny Lopes Cabral in the 103rd minute.

The Blue Sharks were given a hero's welcome upon their return home, paraded through the streets of the capital city Praia. But while life went back to normal for many players, the same could not be said for Vozinha, whose existence has forever been altered by fame.

In a recent interview with The Observer , the now Colo-Colo goalkeeper said, "I've lost my peace and tranquillity. I no longer have any privacy, or at least much less than I used to.

To listen to the latest episode of 'All Out Soccer' - CLICK HERE

"Now I go out, I go to a restaurant, and there's always someone who wants to take a photo with me or asks me for an autograph. Or, worse, someone is filming me. That's what has changed most in my life, and I don't think there's anything I can do about it."

Vozinha's newfound fame has not only come with the disappearance of any sense of anonymity on a daily basis, but it has also presented certain commercial opportunities - something he remains wary of. "I know that during the World Cup there were lots of companies and brands that wanted to work with me," he said, "but while we were competing I only did one promotional collaboration, with UFL Mobile. I don't know what offers might come in the future, but for now I don't want to work with any tobacco, alcohol or betting brands."

Unfortunately, having now sampled both sides of fame, Vozinha has quickly come to realize that it simply isn't for him. "A lot of people want to be famous and have a public profile, but they only see the positive side of that reality," he said. "To be honest, if I were offered the life I have today or the life I had before, I'd choose the one I had before."

But while his prominence has come at a personal cost, he also acknowledges that there have been benefits from a broader perspective, specifically when it comes to his beloved home nation.

Vozinha explained, "It's nice to feel like a kind of ambassador, but I want to make it clear that what we achieved was a collective effort. We made history and the best news would be if we could harness that momentum to develop our country and improve the living conditions of our people."

Now plying his trade in the Chilean top-tier, Vozinha has made three appearances across all competitions, conceding just one goal, with his eyes set on making his Copa Libertadores debut in the near future.

But before then, there remains a chance Vozinha could be named the Men's Goalkeeper of the Year, having been named among the 10 nominees for the award, with the winner set to be announced at the Ballon d'Or ceremony in October.

articles.title: SEC 'regrets' officiating errors during onside kick in Texas-Tennessee game
articles.summary: An onside kick during Texas' game against Tennessee broke a few rules. Here is what would have happened.
articles.body:
Remember the onside kick with 1 minute, 22 seconds left in Texas football 's road game against Tennessee that took an interesting roll, slipped through Ryan Wingo 's hands and gave Tennessee a chance to tie, or take the lead?

Well, the SEC issued a statement Monday morning regretting officiating mistakes. The play should have resulted in a 5-yard penalty and a replay of the down against the Volunteers.

"The Southeastern Conference regrets the error and will continue working with the Secretary/Editor for NCAA Football Rules and officials to ensure consistent application of free-kick rules," the release said.

Dropkicks are allowed, but there are some rules that Tennessee did not abide by. The freekick must be made from "the kicking team's restraining line," the 35-yard line, on the kick unless it is relocated due to a penalty; the ball was kicked from the around the 34-yard line.

Also, there was an issue with the kicker's movement after the ready-to-play signal. According to the rule, after the ball ready for play, a kicker cannot change his lateral position between the hash marks on the field; only after a charged timeout or subsequent kick could they move.

"The kicker's movement after the ready signal violated the rule," the release stated.

A yardage penalty and a replay of the down is the correct course of action if such penalty occurred.

Head coach Steve Sarkisian made a statement on the lack of a penalty during Monday's news conference.

"I don't really have much more to say on that. I've addressed it with the Southeastern Conference. I've addressed it with John McDaid, the head of our officials. They've addressed the issue, so I don't think there's much more to say on that," he said.

Texas safety Jelani McDonald broke up a Hail Mary pass to secure the Longhorns ' 20-17 win to stay undefeated.

articles.title: Esta Italia sí que es la 'Azzurra'
articles.standfirst: Golearon a Turquía (1-4) y dejaron a Montella en la cuerda floja
articles.summary: Golearon a Turquía (1-4) y dejaron a Montella en la cuerda floja
articles.body: Italia, futbolísticamente hablando, sigue estando en ruinas después de perderse los tres últimos Mundiales. El estreno en la Nations ante Bélgica evidenció que Mancini tiene todo por construir en esta segunda etapa. Los primeros cimientos de esta reconstrucción, sin embargo, puede que comiencen a asentarse tras golear a la Turquía (1-4) de un Montella que está en la cuerda floja. La cantidad de hombres que Mancini dejó en Coverciano hacía intuir que iba a darle un lavado de cara a su Italia 2.0: renovó por completo la defensa; Tonali fue el único que se mantuvo en la medular; y Raspadori acompañó arriba a los hermanos Esposito. Algo que no sucedía en la 'Azzurra' desde inicios de siglo con los Inzaghi. Montella, por su parte, repitió el trío de ataque compuesto por Güler, Baris Yilmaz y Uzun. Sin embargo, se vio obligado a dar entrada a Bayindir bajo palos por la expulsión de Çakir ante Francia. Además, Kabak entró en el centro de la defensa, Kökcü entró con Özcan en el doble pivote y Elmali reemplazó a Kadioglü en el carril zurdo. El encuentro no pudo arrancar más de cara para Italia. Cuando apenas habían transcurrido ocho minutos, Bayindir tuvo que estirarse a fondo para desviar a córner un disparo cruzado de Pio Esposito de primeras a la media vuelta. La puso rasa Ruggeri, Celik no acertó a despejar y Bastoni sacó provecho. Con Raspadori tirado a derecha, Mancini formó un rombo en el centro del campo para potenciar la versión más llegadora de un Frattesi que hizo el 0-2 en el 21' después de que Kabak llegase 'in extremis' para desbaratar un mano a mano de Pio. Italia tejió una combinación exquisita en la frontal y, tras la parada de Bayindir a Kayode llegando desde atrás, el centrocampista de la Lazio sacó a relucir su característico olfato. Ni mucho menos quedó la cosa ahí. Italia seguía combinando a una velocidad como hace tiempo que no se veía y, escasos cinco minutos después, Kayode volvió a sorprender irrumpiendo en el área desde el sector derecho. Pio Esposito se hizo grande espaldas y descargó para que el lateral del Brentford resolviese mano a mano. Debut inmejorable para terminar de pedir paso. La primera media hora de Italia había sido un completo vendaval. Antes de irse al descanso, sin embargo, ya habían levantado ligeramente el pie del acelerador y, nada más arrancar la segunda parte, Turquía —Montella introdujo tres cambios— recortó distancias. Ruggeri basculó en exceso, Aydin sirvió un paso atrás desde línea de fondo y Baris Yilmaz empujó a placer. No tardaron en volver los pitos a las gradas de Bursa. Y es que, tan sólo tres minutos más tarde, Italia recuperó la ventaja. Tonali disparó al palo desde la frontal y Pio Esposito recogió el rechace lanzándose en plancha. Así pues, se convirtió en el segundo jugador que más goles ha marcado con la 'Azzurra' (seis) antes de cumplir 21 años. Sólo le supera un mito como Meazza (11). El partido, a partir de entonces, se volvió completamente loco: Yilmaz fue amonestado por simular un penalti ante Donnarumma y, además, desperdició dos servicios brillantes de Güler para recortar distancias. Bayindir, por su parte, evitó que a Turquía le cayese el quinto realizando una doble intervención a Cambiaghi y un Kayode infatigable. Resurgió Italia... aunque deberá ratificarlo contra Francia.
